definition_zh: 使暴露；揭露；使接触到；使遭受（风险）
definition_en: to put something out where it can be seen, known, or affected, with no cover or protection
core_image: 掀开遮盖，把原本藏在里面的东西摆到外面
scene: 仓库货架上堆着发霉的粮袋，记者举着相机。 The reporter photographed the mouldy grain sacks in the warehouse and exposed the hygiene problem of the food factory in one article.
sceneCN: 这里 expose 是「揭露隐秘的不当行为」（第 2 个义项：揭发隐藏的真相）；句意：记者拍下仓库里发霉的粮袋，用一篇报道揭发了这家食品厂的卫生问题。

pos.zh: 使暴露；揭露；使遭受（危险、风险）
使接触；使体验（某种影响）
（亦作 exposé）揭露性报道；曝光文章

collocations.zh: 使某人接触到某物；使某人面临某事

senses.title: Put out in the open: leave uncovered
senses.titleCN: 摆到外面：使不再被遮盖
senses.definition: to put something where it can be seen or reached, after removing whatever covered it
senses.definitionCN: 移开遮盖物，把某物放到能被看见或触及的地方
senses.example: The storm exposed the roots of the old tree.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨把老树的根露了出来。
senses.why: Latin exponere is ex- 'out' + ponere 'to put, place': the thing is literally placed out. The oldest English sense, 'leave without shelter', keeps that picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 exponere 是 ex-“向外”+ ponere“放置”：东西被字面地“放到外面”。英语最早的义项“使无遮蔽”保留的就是这幅画面。

senses.title: Reveal a hidden truth
senses.definition: to make a secret, especially a wrongdoing, known to the public
senses.definitionCN: 使秘密、尤指不当行为为公众所知
senses.example: The investigation exposed serious safety failures at the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 调查揭露了这家工厂严重的安全漏洞。
senses.why: If a fact is 'placed out' where everyone can see it, secrecy ends. The 1620s sense 'exhibit openly' grew into the modern sense of revealing what was kept hidden.
senses.whyCN: 一个事实被“放到外面”让人人都看见，秘密就结束了。17 世纪 20 年代“公开陈列”的义项，后来发展成现代的“揭露被隐藏之事”。

senses.title: Unmask a person
senses.definition: to reveal that someone is not what they claimed to be, usually with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 揭穿某人并非其所自称的样子，通常带有贬义
senses.example: He was exposed as a fraud after the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之后，他被揭穿是个骗子。
senses.why: This is sense 02 applied to a person: the true identity is put out in front of everyone, and the false front can no longer stand.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 2 义项用在人身上：真实身份被摆到众人面前，虚假的外壳就立不住了。

senses.title: Leave unprotected: subject to danger
senses.titleCN: 使失去保护：使遭受危险
senses.definition: to leave someone or something open to harm, attack, or loss
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物处于可能受伤害、攻击或损失的境地
senses.example: The soldiers were exposed to enemy fire for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们数小时暴露在敌军火力之下。
senses.why: To be outside shelter is to have no wall between you and harm. The physical picture of being 'placed out' becomes the military and financial sense of being open to damage.
senses.whyCN: 待在掩体之外，就是你和伤害之间没有墙。'被放到外面'这个物理画面，由此变成军事和金融语境里的“易受损害”。

senses.title: Cause someone to experience something
senses.titleCN: 使某人接触、体验某事物
senses.definition: to give someone the experience of something, especially something new or influential
senses.definitionCN: 让某人经历某事物，尤指新事物或有影响的事物
senses.example: The course exposes students to modern research methods.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课让学生接触到现代研究方法。
senses.why: Being placed next to something is enough for it to act on you. Exposure here is contact, not danger: the person is put within reach of an influence.
senses.whyCN: 被放到某物旁边，就足以让它作用于你。这里的 exposure 是“接触”而非“危险”：人被放进某种影响的作用范围里。

senses.title: Photography: let light reach the film
senses.definition: to allow light to reach photographic film or a digital sensor
senses.definitionCN: 让光线照到胶片或数字传感器上
senses.example: The film was exposed to light before it was developed.
senses.exampleCN: 胶卷在冲洗前就已经曝光了。
senses.why: The photographic sense dates from 1839. Light is 'placed out' onto a sensitive surface, and the image is the trace it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 摄影义项始于 1839 年。光被“放到”感光表面上，影像就是它留下的痕迹。

senses.title: Business: lay open to market risk
senses.titleCN: 商业：使暴露于市场风险
senses.definition: to put a company, currency, or investor in a position where losses are possible
senses.definitionCN: 使公司、货币或投资者处于可能亏损的境地
senses.example: The firm is heavily exposed to currency swings.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司极易受到汇率波动的影响。
senses.why: Finance borrows the physical image: an unprotected position is one standing outside the shelter of a hedge or guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了这个物理画面：没有保护的头寸，就是站在对冲或担保的遮蔽之外。

senses.title: Expose oneself: indecent display
senses.titleCN: 当众裸露：有伤风化的暴露
senses.definition: in law, to display one's genitals indecently in public
senses.definitionCN: 在法律语境中指在公共场所猥亵地裸露身体
senses.example: He was arrested for exposing himself in the park.
senses.exampleCN: 他因在公园里当众裸露而被捕。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the verb back on the body: what is 'placed out' is the person's own uncovered body, and the legal phrase freezes that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把动词转回身体本身：被“放到外面”的是人自己未遮盖的身体，法律短语固定了这一含义。

intro.en: Expose came into English through Old French, where the Latin verb was reshaped by a famous confusion with poser. The Latin base is clear; only the French reshaping needs care.
intro.cn: expose 经古法语进入英语，拉丁动词在法语中因与 poser 的著名混淆而改了形。拉丁词基清楚，需要留意的只是法语这一层改写。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to leave without shelter or defense'. The noun exposé, 'display of discreditable information', appears much later, in 1803, as a French word.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 15 世纪初，义为“使无遮蔽、无防卫”。名词 exposé“揭露不光彩信息”晚得多，1803 年以法语词形进入英语。

items.en: From Old French esposer / exposer 'lay open, set forth, speak one's mind, explain' (13c.). French altered the Latin stem by confusion with poser 'to place, lay down'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 esposer / exposer（13 世纪），意为“敞开、陈述、说出想法、解释”。法语因与 poser“放置、放下”混淆而改写了拉丁词干。

items.en: Latin exponere 'set forth, lay open, exhibit, reveal, publish' = ex- 'out, forth' + ponere 'to put, place'. The past participle expositus is the stem behind exposure and exposition.
items.cn: 拉丁语 exponere“陈列、敞开、展示、揭示、公布”= ex-“向外”+ ponere“放置”。过去分词 expositus 就是 exposure、exposition 的词干。

items.en: Skeat noted that pausare 'to pause, rest' took over the meaning 'to place' in French, so composer, imposer and exposer no longer descend directly from componere, imponere, exponere in form, even though they match them in sense.
items.cn: Skeat 指出，法语中 pausare“暂停、休息”取代了“放置”之义，因此 composer、imposer、exposer 在词形上已不再直接来自 componere、imponere、exponere，尽管词义与它们对应。

items.en: The sense 'exhibit openly' is from the 1620s, 'unmask' from the 1690s, and the photographic sense from 1839. The family keeps ponere alive in compose, depose, impose, propose, postpone and position.
items.cn: “公开陈列”义见于 17 世纪 20 年代，“揭穿”义见于 17 世纪 90 年代，摄影义始于 1839 年。这个词族让 ponere 活在 compose、depose、impose、propose、postpone、position 之中。

note.en: Look-alikes are checked first for form and sound, then near meanings for the exact kind of 'making visible' they name.
note.cn: 先按词形和读音检查形近词，再按“使显现”的具体方式区分近义词。

entries.definition: to explain a theory or belief in detail. It comes from the same exponere 'put out', but English uses it for setting out ideas, not for uncovering secrets.
entries.definitionCN: 详细阐述理论或信仰。它同样来自 exponere“放到外面”，但英语用它“摆出观点”，而不是“揭开秘密”。

entries.definition: the state of being exposed, or the amount of light reaching film. It is the noun of expose, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露的状态，或胶片受光量。它是 expose 的名词派生，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to force something to be accepted. It is in- 'on' + ponere 'place', a sibling of expose rather than a form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 强行施加、征收。它是 in-“在上”+ ponere“放置”，是 expose 的同根兄弟，而不是它的变形。

entries.definition: a newspaper story that reveals a scandal. The accent marks its French origin; without it, expose is the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 揭露丑闻的报道。重音符号标记其法语来源；不带符号时 expose 是动词。

entries.definition: to make something previously unknown visible or known. It is broader and more neutral than expose, which often implies something shameful.
entries.definitionCN: 使原先未知的事物显现或被知道。它比 expose 更宽泛、更中性，而 expose 常暗示不光彩之事。

entries.definition: to make information known, especially in an official or legal setting. It stresses the release of information rather than public shame.
entries.definitionCN: 披露信息，尤用于官方或法律场合。它强调信息的公开，而非公开羞辱。

entries.definition: literally to remove a cover, or figuratively to discover something hidden. It keeps the physical image more strongly than expose.
entries.definitionCN: 字面指揭开覆盖物，引申为发现隐藏之物。它比 expose 更强烈地保留“揭开盖子”的物理意象。

entries.definition: to cause someone or something to undergo a treatment or condition. It matches expose to when the meaning is 'make experience', not 'reveal'.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人某物经受某种对待或状况。当意思是“使经历”而非“揭露”时，它与 expose to 对应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces ex- and ponere and the real English family built on them.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁成分 ex- 与 ponere，以及由它们构成的真实英语词族。

normal.en: ex- means 'out' and ponere means 'place': expose is to place something out, away from its cover.
normal.cn: ex- 意为“向外”，ponere 意为“放置”：expose 就是把东西放到外面、离开遮盖。

normal.en: Exposition is literally a 'placing out' of ideas; expound is the same root used for explaining.
normal.cn: exposition 字面就是“把观点摆出来”；expound 用同一词根表示“阐述”。

normal.en: Exposure is the noun: a photographic exposure places light onto film for a measured time.
normal.cn: exposure 是名词：摄影曝光就是把光在规定时间内放到胶片上。

normal.en: An exposé is a news story that brings a hidden scandal out where the public can see it.
normal.cn: exposé 是把隐藏丑闻摆到公众眼前的新闻报道。

normal.en: Be exposed to something is to be placed in contact with it, from music to disease.
normal.cn: be exposed to something 就是被放进与某物的接触范围，从音乐到疾病都适用。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain pulled back: what was behind it is now in the open, and that is expose.
abstract.cn: 想象一块幕布被拉开：原本在后面的东西现在到了明处，这就是 expose。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing outside a shelter in the rain: the same removal of cover becomes exposure to danger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在雨中、没有遮蔽：同样的“去掉遮盖”就变成暴露于危险。

abstract.en: Picture a beam of light hitting film: the thing placed out is not a secret but light itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光打在胶片上：被“放到外面”的不是秘密，而是光本身。

examples.en: Do not expose the battery to direct sunlight for long periods.
examples.cn: 不要让电池长时间暴露在直射阳光下。

examples.en: The documentary exposed conditions in the city's shelters.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片刻画并揭露了该市收容所里的状况。

examples.en: Children exposed to two languages early often switch between them easily.
examples.cn: 早期接触两种语言的儿童往往能轻松切换。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗死剖姿”——把摆好的姿势剖开、摊到门外给人看 → expose 暴露、揭露

root: 拉丁 ex-“向外”+ ponere“放置”，字面是“放到外面”，因此核心义是“使暴露、使显现”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of expose all come from one act: taking something out of its cover. What is taken out may be an object, a truth, a person, a body, or a beam of light.
sensesIntro.cn: expose 的八个义项都来自同一个动作：把东西从遮盖中拿出来。被拿出来的可以是物件、真相、人、身体，也可以是一束光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cover is removed and something is placed outside where it can be seen or reached.
core.cn: 核心意象：遮盖被移除，某物被放到外面，可以被看见或触及。

branches.en: VISIBLE: an object or a photographic surface is simply put out where light or eyes can reach it.
branches.cn: 可见：物件或感光表面被放到光线与目光能够到达的地方。

branches.en: KNOWN: the thing placed out is information, and once it is out, secrecy or a false identity collapses.
branches.cn: 被知晓：被放到外面的是信息；一旦出来，秘密或虚假身份就崩塌。

branches.en: UNPROTECTED: without a cover or a hedge, the exposed thing can be hit by fire, weather, or losses.
branches.cn: 无保护：没有遮盖或对冲，暴露之物就可能被火力、天气或亏损击中。

branches.en: CONTACT: being placed next to an influence is enough for it to act on you.
branches.cn: 接触：被放到某种影响旁边，就足以让它作用于你。

branches.en: BODY: the reflexive form exposes the person's own uncovered body, fixed in legal usage.
branches.cn: 身体：反身形式暴露的是人自己未遮盖的身体，并在法律用法中固定下来。

intro.en: Expose is ex- 'out' plus the Latin verb ponere 'place', reshaped in French. English adds ordinary suffixes: -ure for the noun, -ed for the adjective, -é for the French-style noun.
intro.cn: expose 是 ex-“向外”加拉丁动词 ponere“放置”，在法语中改形。英语只加普通后缀：-ure 构成名词，-ed 构成形容词，-é 构成法语式名词。

latinIntro.en: The ponere family is large and regular: componere, deponere, imponere, proponere, postponere, expositio. Note that French poser, from pausare, replaced the form while keeping the sense.
latinIntro.cn: ponere 词族庞大而规则：componere、deponere、imponere、proponere、postponere、expositio。要注意法语 poser 来自 pausare，替换了词形却保留了词义。

items.meaning: to place out; to uncover or reveal
items.meaningCN: 放到外面；使暴露、揭露（ex-“向外”+ ponere“放置”）
items.example: The report exposes how the money was moved.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告揭露了资金是如何被转移的。

items.meaning: the state of being exposed; the amount of light reaching film
items.meaningCN: 暴露；曝光；曝光量（-ure 构成动作或状态名词）
items.example: Long exposure to the sun damages the skin.
items.exampleCN: 长时间日晒会损伤皮肤。

items.meaning: left without cover or protection
items.meaningCN: 无遮蔽的；暴露在外的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The exposed pipes froze overnight.
items.exampleCN: 裸露在外的管道一夜之间冻住了。

items.meaning: a revealing report, usually about a scandal
items.meaningCN: 揭露性报道，通常关于丑闻（法语过去分词借入）
items.example: The magazine published an exposé on the charity.
items.exampleCN: 杂志刊登了一篇揭露该慈善机构的报道。

items.meaning: a full public display or explanation of an idea
items.meaningCN: 阐述；博览会（ex- + posit-“放置”+ -ion 名词后缀）
items.example: The first chapter is a clear exposition of the theory.
items.exampleCN: 第一章清晰地阐述了这一理论。

items.meaning: intended to explain or set out information
items.meaningCN: 说明性的；解释性的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: Expository writing explains rather than tells a story.
items.exampleCN: 说明文重在解释，而不是讲故事。

items.meaning: to expose too much, especially to light
items.meaningCN: 使曝光过度；使过度暴露（over-“过度”）
items.example: The sky was overexposed in that photo.
items.exampleCN: 那张照片里的天空曝光过度了。

items.meaning: to expose too little, so the image is too dark
items.meaningCN: 使曝光不足，导致影像过暗（under-“不足”）
items.example: The portrait was underexposed and hard to see.
items.exampleCN: 那张肖像曝光不足，很难看清。

items.meaning: able to be exposed or revealed
items.meaningCN: 可暴露的；可揭露的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The data set is exposable only after review.
items.exampleCN: 该数据集只有经过审查后才能公开。

latinEntries.meaning: to set forth, lay open, exhibit, reveal
latinEntries.meaningCN: 陈列；敞开；展示；揭示（expose 的直接拉丁来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：他把书摊在桌上。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 放置；安放（过去分词 positus 生成 position、positive）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：他把容器放在地上。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 陈述；解释；展出（英语 exposition 的直接来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：对观点的阐述。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 放在上面；施加（英语 impose 的来源，与 expose 同根）

definition_zh: 外部的；外面的；外来的；表面的
definition_en: belonging to or coming from the outside, rather than the inside of something
core_image: 一堵墙的外侧：所有在墙体之外的东西
scene: 医生把外用的药膏涂在伤口上，标签上写着 for external use only。
sceneCN: 这里 external 是「外用的、作用于体表的」（第 5 个义项：医学上的外用）；句意：医生把外用药膏涂在伤口上，标签写着“仅供外用”。图中可辨识物件：药膏管、伤口、纱布、外用标签。

pos.zh: 外来的；外国的；组织外的

senses.title: On the outside surface
senses.definition: situated on or forming the outer surface of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的外表面，或构成其外表面
senses.example: The external walls of the house need repainting.
senses.exampleCN: 房子的外墙需要重新粉刷。
senses.why: Latin externus means 'outside, outward', built on exterus, the comparative of ex 'out of'. The word starts from the boundary line: whatever is on the far side of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 externus 意为“外面的、向外的”，由 ex“出”的比较级 exterus 构成。这个词从边界线开始：凡是位于界线之外的东西。

senses.title: Coming from outside
senses.definition: originating outside a person, group, or system rather than within it
senses.definitionCN: 来自人、群体或系统之外，而非其内部
senses.example: The decision was made under external pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定是在外部压力下作出的。
senses.why: Once the word names a boundary, anything crossing it from the far side is external. The cause is located outside the thing affected.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词命名了边界，凡是从另一侧越过边界而来的东西就是 external。原因被定位在被影响之物以外。

senses.title: Foreign: outside the country or organization
senses.definition: relating to another country or to people outside an organization
senses.definitionCN: 与另一国家有关，或与组织之外的人有关
senses.example: The country's external debt rose sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 该国的外债急剧上升。
senses.why: A national border is the largest version of the same boundary. What lies beyond it is external, so the word serves for foreign affairs and foreign debt.
senses.whyCN: 国界是同一条边界的最大版本。位于国界之外的就是 external，因此这个词用于“对外事务”和“外债”。

senses.title: Outward and superficial
senses.definition: belonging only to appearance, not to the true inner nature
senses.definitionCN: 只属于外表，而非真正的内在本质
senses.example: His external calm hid deep anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他表面的平静掩盖着深深的愤怒。
senses.why: If the inner self is the core, then what shows on the outside is only a surface layer. External here contrasts with essential or internal.
senses.whyCN: 若内心是核心，那么显露在外面的就只是一层表面。这里的 external 与“本质的、内在的”相对。

senses.title: Medicine: for external use
senses.definition: applied to the outside of the body rather than swallowed or injected
senses.definitionCN: 施用于体表，而非吞服或注射
senses.example: This ointment is for external use only.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药膏仅供外用。
senses.why: Medicine maps the body as a container: a remedy applied to the skin stays on the outer surface and does not enter the interior.
senses.whyCN: 医学把身体看作一个容器：涂在皮肤上的药物停留在外表面，不进入内部。

senses.title: Computing: outside the main device
senses.definition: connected to a computer from outside its main case
senses.definitionCN: 从主机箱外部连接到计算机
senses.example: He backed up the files to an external drive.
senses.exampleCN: 他把文件备份到了外置硬盘。
senses.why: The computer case is treated as the boundary. A device plugged in from beyond that case is external, even though it is part of the working system.
senses.whyCN: 机箱被当作边界。从机箱之外接入的设备就是 external，即使它是工作系统的一部分。

senses.title: Independent: from outside the institution
senses.definition: done or provided by someone not belonging to the organization being judged
senses.definitionCN: 由不属于被评审机构的第三方完成或提供
senses.example: An external auditor reviewed the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 一位外部审计师审查了账目。
senses.why: Being outside the organization is a guarantee of independence: the examiner has no internal loyalty that could blur the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 身处组织之外是独立性的保证：评审人没有可能模糊判断的内部忠诚。

senses.title: Noun: outward appearances
senses.definition: in the plural, outward appearances or non-essential details
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指外在表象或非本质的细节
senses.example: The report cares about externals rather than causes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注的是外在表象，而不是原因。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the set of things that are outside: appearances, formalities, and surface details.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为名词，指所有处于外部的东西：外表、礼节和表面细节。

intro.en: External is a Latin adjective built on the comparative exterus 'outer', itself from ex 'out of'. The family is regular and the etymology is not in doubt.
intro.cn: external 是拉丁形容词，建立在比较级 exterus“外面的”之上，后者来自 ex“出”。词族规则，词源没有疑问。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'overt' (open, not hidden); by the 1590s it means 'situated or lying outside'.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 15 世纪初，义为“公开的、不隐藏的”；到 16 世纪 90 年代，义为“位于外面”。

items.en: Latin externus 'outside, outward' = exterus 'on the outside, outer, foreign' + -nus, an adjective ending. Exterus is a comparative of ex 'out of'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 externus“外面的、向外的”= exterus“在外、外部的、外国的”+ 形容词后缀 -nus。exterus 是 ex“出”的比较级。

items.en: The comparative series exterior 'more outward' and extremus 'outermost' belongs to the same stem; English later borrowed exterior and extreme from it.
items.cn: 比较级序列 exterior“更靠外的”和 extremus“最外面的”属于同一词干；英语后来借入了 exterior 和 extreme。

items.en: External competed with the older form exterial; external won and produced externally. The noun extern, 'outsider, day-scholar', entered from French in the 16th century.
items.cn: external 与更早的 exterial 竞争，最终胜出并产生副词 externally。名词 extern“外人、走读生”在 16 世纪从法语进入英语。

items.en: The word now covers walls, affairs, devices, auditors and medicines. All are applications of one spatial contrast: inside versus outside a boundary.
items.cn: 现代英语中它覆盖墙体、事务、设备、审计师和药物。所有这些都应用了同一个空间对比：边界之内与边界之外。

note.en: First separate the spelling neighbours from words that also mean 'outside', then check whether each points to position, origin, or appearance.
note.cn: 先把拼写相近的词与同样表示“外面”的词分开，再看各自指向位置、来源还是外表。

entries.definition: lasting forever. It shares the -ernal ending but comes from aeternus, with no relation to externus.
entries.definitionCN: 永恒的。它有相同的 -ernal 结尾，但来自 aeternus，与 externus 无关。

entries.definition: the outer surface or appearance. It is the comparative of exterus, so it stresses the surface rather than the whole outside world.
entries.definitionCN: 外部表面或外观。它是 exterus 的比较级，因此强调表面，而不是整个外部世界。

entries.definition: belonging to the inside. It is built on internus 'within', the mirror image of externus.
entries.definitionCN: 内部的。它由 internus“在内”构成，是 externus 的镜像对应词。

entries.definition: an outsider, or a day-scholar who is not a boarder. It is a noun borrowed from French, not a short form of external in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 外人；走读生。它是从法语借入的名词，词源上并不是 external 的缩写。

entries.definition: further from the centre; on the outside. It is simpler and more physical than external, and rarely means 'foreign'.
entries.definitionCN: 离中心更远的；外面的。它比 external 更简单、更具体，而且很少表示“外国的”。

entries.definition: going or pointing away from the inside. It stresses direction of movement, while external stresses belonging to the outside.
entries.definitionCN: 向外的；朝外的。它强调运动方向，而 external 强调属于外部。

entries.definition: belonging to another country. It is narrower than external and cannot describe a hard drive or a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 属于另一个国家的。它比 external 范围窄，不能形容硬盘或墙体。

entries.definition: coming from outside and not essential or relevant. It adds the idea of unwanted extra material.
entries.definitionCN: 外来的，且非必要或不相关的。它额外带有多余、不相干的意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin contrast exterus / internus and the real derived family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁对比 exterus / internus，以及真实的派生词族。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + -ternus: external things sit on the far side of the boundary, while internal things sit inside it.
normal.cn: ex-“向外”+ -ternus：external 的东西在边界之外，internal 的东西在边界之内。

normal.en: External and interior share the same exterus stem; exterior is the surface, external is the whole outside relation.
normal.cn: external 与 interior 共享 exterus 词干；exterior 是表面，external 是整体的外部关系。

normal.en: An external examiner is outside the school; an external drive is outside the case; external affairs are outside the country.
normal.cn: external examiner 在学校之外；external drive 在机箱之外；external affairs 在国家之外。

normal.en: For external use only is a label that keeps a medicine outside the body.
normal.cn: for external use only 这个标签把药物留在体表之外。

normal.en: Externals are the outside appearances that a serious report should look past.
normal.cn: externals 是严肃报告应当看穿的外在表象。

abstract.en: Picture a building wall: everything beyond the wall is external, everything within it is internal, and the wall itself is the exterior.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵建筑外墙：墙外的一切是 external，墙内的一切是 internal，而墙本身是 exterior。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow crossing the wall from outside to inside: the arrow is an external influence entering the system.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭从墙外穿入墙内：这支箭就是进入系统的外部影响。

abstract.en: Picture a calm face over a storm of feelings: the face is the external layer, the storm is the internal reality.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平静的脸下翻涌着情绪：脸是 external 的表层，情绪是 internal 的真实。

examples.en: External conditions can change faster than a plan can adapt.
examples.cn: 外部条件的变化可能比计划的调整更快。

examples.en: The medicine is safe but must not be taken internally; it is external only.
examples.cn: 这种药安全，但不可内服，只能外用。

examples.en: External evidence should be weighed against what the theory predicts.
examples.cn: 外部证据应当与理论的预测相权衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一克斯特呢”——站在“外面”的人回头喊：特呢？特在外面呢 → external 外部的

root: 拉丁 exterus“外面的”（ex“出”的比较级）+ 形容词后缀 -nus，核心是“边界之外”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of external all apply one spatial contrast. A wall, a country, a body, a computer case, and an institution each draw a boundary, and external names what lies beyond it.
sensesIntro.cn: external 的八个义项都应用同一个空间对比。墙、国家、身体、机箱、机构各自画出一条边界，external 指边界之外的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary line, and everything that lies on the far side of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界线，以及位于线另一侧的一切。

branches.en: OBJECT BOUNDARIES: walls, skin, and a computer case each define an outside surface.
branches.cn: 物体边界：墙、皮肤、机箱都界定出一个外表面。

branches.en: GROUP BOUNDARIES: pressures, debts and demands come from beyond the group's own line.
branches.cn: 群体边界：压力、债务与要求来自群体自身界线之外。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: what shows on the surface is external, as opposed to the inner essence.
branches.cn: 外表：显露在表面的是 external，与内在本质相对。

branches.en: INDEPENDENCE: an examiner outside the institution is trusted precisely because of that outside position.
branches.cn: 独立：机构之外的评审人，正因身处其外而获得信任。

branches.en: FOREIGN: the national border turns the same contrast into the foreign country or the outside organisation.
branches.cn: 外国的：国界把同一种对比变成“外国的”，即本国或本组织之外。

intro.en: External is a Latin adjective in -al added to externus. The productive English suffixes are -ly for the adverb, -ity for the abstract noun, and -ize for the verb.
intro.cn: external 是拉丁形容词，在 externus 后加 -al。英语中能产的后缀有 -ly（副词）、-ity（抽象名词）、-ize（动词）。

latinIntro.en: The stem is exter- 'outer', a comparative of ex. Latin exterior and extremus belong here; internus 'within' is the exact mirror.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 exter-“外面的”，是 ex 的比较级。拉丁语 exterior 与 extremus 都属于这里；internus“在内”是精确的镜像词。

items.meaning: belonging to the outside
items.meaningCN: 外部的（externus + -al 构成形容词）
items.example: External walls face the street.
items.exampleCN: 外墙朝向街道。

items.meaning: in relation to the outside; from the outside
items.meaningCN: 在外部；从外部（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The building was externally inspected.
items.exampleCN: 这栋建筑接受了外部检查。

items.meaning: a cost or benefit that falls on a third party
items.meaningCN: 外部性；由第三方承担的成本或收益（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: Pollution is a classic negative externality.
items.exampleCN: 污染是典型的负外部性。

items.meaning: to make something outward or visible
items.meaningCN: 使外化；使表现于外（-ize 表示“使成为”）
items.example: Children externalize feelings through play.
items.exampleCN: 儿童通过游戏把情绪外化。

items.meaning: the process of making something outward
items.meaningCN: 外化；外在化（-ation 构成动作名词）
items.example: The externalization of memory into devices is common.
items.exampleCN: 把记忆外化到设备中很常见。

items.structure: Latin externus used as a noun
items.meaning: an outsider; a day-scholar
items.meaningCN: 外人；走读生（externus 的名词用法）
items.example: The externs leave school at five.
items.exampleCN: 走读生五点离校。

items.meaning: the outer surface or appearance
items.meaningCN: 外部；外观（exter- + 比较级后缀 -ior）
items.example: The exterior of the car was undamaged.
items.exampleCN: 汽车的外部没有受损。

items.meaning: the furthest or most intense point
items.meaningCN: 极端的；极度的（来自 extremus“最外面的”）
items.example: The extreme heat closed the school.
items.exampleCN: 极端高温使学校停课。

items.meaning: belonging to the inside
items.meaningCN: 内部的（internus“在内”+ -al，external 的镜像词）
items.example: The internal walls are painted white.
items.exampleCN: 内墙被漆成白色。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 外面的；向外的（external 的直接拉丁来源）
在外面的；外部的；外国的（ex 的比较级形式）
更靠外的；外面的（英语 exterior 的来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：外面那一部分。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 最外面的；最后的；极端的（英语 extreme 的来源）

definition_en: to draw or pull something out, or the substance or passage that has been drawn out
core_image: 从材料深处把东西拉出来
scene: 牙科椅上，病人张着嘴，托盘里放着牙钳和纱布。 The dentist extracted the bad tooth with forceps and then asked the patient to bite on a gauze pad.
sceneCN: 这里 extract 是「拔出、取出」（第 1 个义项：把东西从原处拉出，尤指牙或异物）；句意：牙医用钳子拔掉了那颗坏牙，然后让病人咬住纱布止血。

pos.zh: 提取物；浓缩物；摘录；节选

senses.title: Pull something out physically
senses.titleCN: 物理拔出：把东西从原处拉出
senses.definition: to remove something by pulling it out, especially from the body or the ground
senses.definitionCN: 通过拉拽取出某物，尤指从身体或地下取出
senses.example: The dentist extracted two bad teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医拔掉了两颗坏牙。
senses.why: Latin extrahere is ex- 'out' + trahere 'to draw, pull'. The word is a physical pulling, and the object starts inside something else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 extrahere 是 ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉、拖”。这个词就是物理性的拉拽，而对象起初在别的东西里面。

senses.title: Obtain by force or effort
senses.definition: to obtain information, money, or a promise from someone who does not give it easily
senses.definitionCN: 从不愿轻易给予的人那里取得信息、金钱或许诺
senses.example: The officers extracted a confession from the suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 警员从嫌疑人那里逼出了供词。
senses.why: The physical pull becomes social pressure: what is wanted is held inside a resistant person, and effort is needed to draw it out.
senses.whyCN: 物理的拉拽变成社会压力：想要的东西被一个不情愿的人握在手里，必须用力才能拉出来。

senses.title: Chemistry: separate a substance
senses.definition: to obtain a substance from a mixture by chemical or physical means
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学或物理方法从混合物中取得某种物质
senses.example: The plant extracts oil from the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂从种子中提取油。
senses.why: In extraction one component is drawn out of a mixture and left separate. The Latin pull now happens at the level of molecules.
senses.whyCN: 萃取时，一个成分被从混合物中拉出来并单独留下。拉丁语的“拉”现在发生在分子层面。

senses.title: Take a passage from a text
senses.definition: to select and copy a passage from a longer written work
senses.definitionCN: 从较长的文字作品中选取并抄录一段
senses.example: She extracted a paragraph from the report to use as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她从报告中摘录了一段作为证据。
senses.why: A passage is pulled out of its context just as a tooth is pulled out of a jaw. What remains behind is the surrounding text.
senses.whyCN: 一段文字被从上下文中拉出来，正如牙齿被从牙床里拔出来。留在后面的是周围的文本。

senses.title: Derive meaning from data
senses.definition: to obtain a meaning, pattern, or value from information that is not obvious at first
senses.definitionCN: 从起初并不明显的信息中得出意义、模式或数值
senses.example: Analysts extracted a clear trend from the raw numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师从原始数字中得出了一个清晰的趋势。
senses.why: The useful result is buried in the material and must be drawn out. This is the intellectual version of chemical extraction.
senses.whyCN: 有用的结果埋在材料里，必须被拉出来。这是化学萃取在智力层面的版本。

senses.title: Noun: a short excerpt
senses.definition: a short passage taken from a book, speech, or document
senses.definitionCN: 从书、演讲或文件中取出的一小段文字
senses.example: The article opened with an extract from her diary.
senses.exampleCN: 文章以她日记中的一段节选开头。
senses.why: The noun is the thing that has been pulled out. English has used extract for an excerpt since the 17th century.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是被拉出来的那个东西。英语从 17 世纪起就用 extract 表示“摘录”。

senses.title: Noun: a concentrated substance
senses.definition: a concentrated preparation made by extracting the useful part of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 通过提取某物质的有效成分而制成的浓缩制品
senses.example: Add a teaspoon of vanilla extract to the batter.
senses.exampleCN: 往面糊里加一茶匙香草精。
senses.why: Here the noun names the product of sense 03: the drawn-out essence, reduced and concentrated in a bottle.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词指第 3 义项的产物：被拉出来的精华，经过浓缩装进瓶子里。

senses.title: Noun: origin or ancestry
senses.definition: in the phrase of ... extraction, the social or national origin of a person
senses.definitionCN: 用于 of ... extraction，指某人的社会或民族出身
senses.example: She is a scientist of Italian extraction.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位意大利血统的科学家。
senses.why: A person is imagined as coming out of a family or country, the way a substance comes out of its source material.
senses.whyCN: 人被想象为从某个家族或国家“出来”，就像物质从其原料中出来一样。

senses.title: Mathematics: extract a root
senses.definition: to calculate a root of a number, as in 'extract the square root'
senses.definitionCN: 求某数的方根，如 extract the square root（开平方）
senses.example: Students learned to extract the square root without a calculator.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们学会了不用计算器开平方。
senses.why: The root is treated as hidden inside the number and drawn out by calculation. The metaphor is old and survives as a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 方根被看作藏在数字内部，通过计算被拉出来。这个比喻很古老，并作为固定说法保留下来。

intro.en: The etymonline page for extract could not be retrieved during this batch, so the account below follows the standard Latin derivation, which is not disputed: ex- 'out' + trahere 'draw, pull'.
intro.cn: 本批抓取 etymonline 的 extract 页面连续失败，以下采用通行且无争议的拉丁语推导：ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉、拖”。

items.en: The verb appears in English in the mid-15th century from Latin extractus, past participle of extrahere. The noun for an excerpt follows in the 17th century.
items.cn: 动词于 15 世纪中期从拉丁语 extractus（extrahere 的过去分词）进入英语。表示“摘录”的名词在 17 世纪出现。

items.en: extrahere 'draw out' = ex- 'out' + trahere 'to draw, drag, pull'. The participle stem extract- supplies the English verb and noun.
items.cn: extrahere“拉出”= ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉、拖、拽”。分词词干 extract- 提供了英语的动词和名词。

items.en: Trahere also gives tractor, traction, abstract, attract, contract, distract, protract and subtract, all built on the image of pulling.
items.cn: trahere 还产生 tractor、traction、abstract、attract、contract、distract、protract、subtract，全部建立在“拉”的意象上。

items.en: The chemical sense of obtaining a substance by separation and the noun sense of a concentrated preparation both settle in English usage.
items.cn: 通过分离取得物质的化学义，以及表示浓缩制品的名词义，都在英语用法中稳定下来。

items.en: The family splits into the physical pull (tooth, ore), the informational pull (data, confession) and the product (vanilla extract).
items.cn: 这个词族分成物理拉取（牙齿、矿石）、信息拉取（数据、供词）和产物（香草精）三类。

note.en: Look-alikes are separated by their Latin prefix, near meanings by whether the pulling is physical, chemical, or textual.
note.cn: 形近词按拉丁前缀区分，近义词按“拉取”是物理、化学还是文本层面区分。

entries.definition: as a noun the stress moves to the first syllable. The spelling is unchanged, so listen for the stress to tell verb from noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作名词时重音移到第一音节。拼写不变，因此要靠重音区分动词和名词。

entries.definition: to draw away or summarize; also an academic summary. It is abs- 'away' + trahere, so the pulling goes away from the thing rather than out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 抽取；概括；摘要。它是 abs-“离开”+ trahere，拉的方向是离开原物，而不是从原物中出来。

entries.definition: to draw someone or something toward you. It is at- 'to' + trahere, the opposite direction from extract.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引。它是 at-“向”+ trahere，方向与 extract 相反。

entries.definition: the act of extracting, or a person's origin. It is the noun from extract, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 提取行为，或人的出身。它是 extract 的名词派生，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to take something away from a place. It is neutral and broad; extract adds effort and the idea of drawing from inside.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某处拿走。它中性而宽泛；extract 则增加“费力”和“从内部拉出”的意思。

entries.definition: to take back or pull out, especially money or troops. It stresses retreat or removal, not extraction of an essence.
entries.definitionCN: 撤回；取回，尤指钱或军队。它强调撤退或移除，而不是提取精华。

entries.definition: to obtain something from a source, especially an idea or word. It matches extract in the data and origin senses but not the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 从来源获得，尤指观点或词语。它在“数据”和“出身”义项上与 extract 对应，但不能指物理拔出。

entries.definition: a short passage taken from a longer work. It is almost the same as extract as a noun, but it cannot mean a chemical product.
entries.definitionCN: 从较长作品中取出的短段。作名词时几乎等同于 extract，但不能指化学提取物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces ex- and trahere and the real English family built on traction.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁成分 ex- 与 trahere，以及建立在“拉”意象上的真实英语词族。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + trahere 'pull': extract is a pull outward, from a tooth to a confession.
normal.cn: ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉”：extract 就是向外拉，从牙齿到供词都适用。

normal.en: Tractor, traction and extract share the same pulling stem; a tractor pulls, and extraction pulls something out.
normal.cn: tractor、traction、extract 共享同一个“拉”的词干；拖拉机在拉，提取是把某物拉出来。

normal.en: Attract pulls toward, abstract pulls away, extract pulls out: the prefix tells the direction.
normal.cn: attract 往这边拉，abstract 拉走，extract 拉出来：前缀决定方向。

normal.en: An extract of a book is a passage pulled out of the surrounding text.
normal.cn: 书的一则 extract 就是从周围文本中拉出来的一段。

normal.en: Vanilla extract is the drawn-out essence of the bean, concentrated in a small bottle.
normal.cn: 香草精是被拉出来的香草豆精华，浓缩在一只小瓶里。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of tongs reaching into a jar and lifting one object out: that single lifted object is the extract.
abstract.cn: 想象一把夹子伸进罐子里夹出一个东西：被夹出的那一个就是 extract。

abstract.en: Picture water being pulled up through a straw: the useful part is drawn out and the rest stays behind.
abstract.cn: 想象水被吸管吸上来：有用的部分被拉出，其余留在原处。

abstract.en: Picture a miner separating metal from rock: the pull is now chemical, and the product is the purified extract.
abstract.cn: 想象矿工从岩石中分离金属：这时的“拉”是化学性的，产物就是提纯后的 extract。

examples.en: The software can extract text from scanned images.
examples.cn: 这款软件能从扫描图像中提取文字。

examples.en: The interview was published as an extract from a longer memoir.
examples.cn: 这篇访谈是作为一部较长回忆录的节选发表的。

examples.en: It is hard to extract a fair conclusion from such incomplete records.
examples.cn: 从如此不完整的记录中得出公正的结论是很难的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一克斯拽克特”——往外一拽就把它拽出来 → extract 拔出、提取

root: 拉丁 ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉、拖”，字面是“往外拉”，因此核心义是“拔出、提取”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of extract all use one gesture: a hand pulls something out of the material that holds it. The material may be a jaw, a mixture, a text, a data set, or a family.
sensesIntro.cn: extract 的九个义项都使用同一个动作：一只手把东西从包住它的材料里拉出来。材料可以是牙床、混合物、文本、数据集，也可以是家族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is held inside a larger mass, and force draws it out.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被包在更大的物质里，力量把它拉出来。

branches.en: PULLING OUT: a tooth leaves the jaw, a passage leaves the text, and a root is drawn out of a number.
branches.cn: 拉出：牙离开牙床，段落离开正文，方根则从一个数里被开出来。

branches.en: RESISTANCE: when the holder will not give, the pull becomes pressure.
branches.cn: 阻力：当持有者不愿给时，拉取就变成施压。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: chemistry separates one component, and the noun names the concentrated product.
branches.cn: 物质：化学把一个成分分离出来，名词则指浓缩后的产物。

branches.en: MEANING: the pattern is buried in the data and must be drawn out by analysis.
branches.cn: 意义：模式埋在数据里，必须通过分析把它拉出来。

branches.en: EXCERPT AND ORIGIN: both are things that come out of a larger source and are identified by that source.
branches.cn: 摘录与出身：两者都是从更大来源中出来的东西，并借助该来源被界定。

intro.en: Extract is ex- plus the Latin verb trahere. English suffixes build abstract nouns (-ion), agents (-or), abilities (-able) and adjectives (-ive).
intro.cn: extract 是 ex- 加拉丁动词 trahere。英语后缀构成抽象名词（-ion）、施动者（-or）、能力（-able）和形容词（-ive）。

latinIntro.en: Trahere 'to draw, pull' has a large Latin family: tractus 'a drawing', tractor 'one who draws', distractus, abstractus, attractus. The participle stem tract- is what English borrows.
latinIntro.cn: trahere“拉、拖”有庞大的拉丁词族：tractus“拉”、tractor“拉的人”、distractus、abstractus、attractus。英语借入的是分词词干 tract-。

items.meaning: to draw out; a drawn-out essence or passage
items.meaningCN: 拉出；提取物；摘录（ex-“向外”+ trahere“拉”）
items.example: They extract salt from seawater.
items.exampleCN: 他们从海水中提取盐。

items.meaning: the act of drawing something out; origin
items.meaningCN: 提取；拔出；出身（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The extraction of the tooth took ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 拔牙用了十分钟。

items.meaning: a device or person that extracts
items.meaningCN: 提取器；抽油烟机；提取者（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The kitchen extractor removes steam.
items.exampleCN: 厨房抽油烟机排出蒸汽。

items.meaning: relating to extraction, especially of natural resources
items.meaningCN: 提取的；采掘的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Extractive industries dig and drill.
items.exampleCN: 采掘业从事挖掘和钻探。

items.meaning: able to be extracted
items.meaningCN: 可提取的；可拔出的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The oil is extractable at low cost.
items.exampleCN: 这种油可以低成本提取。

items.meaning: a substance used to extract another substance
items.meaningCN: 萃取剂（-ant 表示起作用的物质）
items.example: The lab added a solvent extractant.
items.exampleCN: 实验室加入了一种溶剂萃取剂。

items.meaning: to draw away; existing as an idea rather than a thing
items.meaningCN: 抽取；抽象的（abs-“离开”+ trahere“拉”）
items.example: Beauty is an abstract idea.
items.exampleCN: 美是一个抽象概念。

items.meaning: to draw toward
items.meaningCN: 吸引（at-“向”+ trahere“拉”）
items.example: The bright sign attracted customers.
items.exampleCN: 明亮的招牌吸引了顾客。

items.meaning: to draw together; a binding agreement
items.meaningCN: 收缩；合同（con-“一起”+ trahere“拉”）
items.example: Metal contracts when it cools.
items.exampleCN: 金属冷却时会收缩。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉；拖；拽（extract、attract、contract 的共同词根）
抽出；拉出（英语 extract 的直接拉丁来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：他把水抽出来。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉；走向；地带（英语 tract、traction 的来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：长长的一片地带。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被拉走的；抽象的（英语 abstract 的来源）

definition_zh: 因素；要素；因子；倍数；代理人
definition_en: one of the things that contributes to a result, or a number that divides another exactly
core_image: 同时推动一件事的几只手
scene: 战术板上贴着磁吸棋子，旁边画着天气图标。 The coach circled fitness, teamwork, and weather on the tactics board and called them the three factors that decide a match.
sceneCN: 这里 factor 是「因素、要素」（第 1 个义项：影响结果的要素）；句意：教练在战术板上圈出体能、配合和天气，称它们是决定比赛的三个因素。

pos.zh: 把……作为因素计入（factor in）；分解因子（factor out）

senses.title: A contributor to a result
senses.definition: one of the conditions or elements that helps produce a result
senses.definitionCN: 促成某一结果的条件或要素之一
senses.example: Cost was the main factor in their decision.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是他们作决定的主要因素。
senses.why: The modern sense grew from the mathematical one in 1816: just as numbers multiply to make a product, circumstances combine to make an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 现代义项在 1816 年从数学义发展而来：正如数字相乘得到积，各种情况也组合成一个结果。

senses.title: Mathematics: a number that divides another
senses.titleCN: 数学：能整除另一个数的因数
senses.definition: a whole number that divides another number exactly, leaving no remainder
senses.definitionCN: 能整除另一个数、不留余数的整数
senses.example: Three and five are factors of fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 3 和 5 是 15 的因数。
senses.why: The mathematical sense is recorded from the 1670s. Factors are the numbers that build a product, which is why the word later meant anything that helps build a result.
senses.whyCN: 数学义记录于 17 世纪 70 年代。因数是构成乘积的数字，这就是为什么这个词后来指任何促成结果的要素。

senses.title: A multiplier: how many times larger
senses.titleCN: 倍数：增大或缩小的量级
senses.definition: a quantity by which another quantity is multiplied, as in 'larger by a factor of ten'
senses.definitionCN: 用以乘另一数量的量，如“大十倍”中的倍数
senses.example: The new machine is faster by a factor of three.
senses.exampleCN: 新机器的速度快了三倍。
senses.why: This keeps the mathematical core visible: one quantity is scaled by another, and the factor tells the scaling.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留了数学核心：一个数量被另一个数量缩放，而 factor 说明缩放的比例。

senses.title: Biology and medicine: a agent in the body
senses.titleCN: 生物医学：体内起作用的因子
senses.definition: a substance, gene, or condition that produces a biological effect
senses.definitionCN: 在生物体内产生某种效应的物质、基因或条件
senses.example: Vitamin C is a factor in collagen production.
senses.exampleCN: 维生素 C 是胶原蛋白生成的一个因子。
senses.why: Science uses factor for an unnamed or newly identified agent that contributes to a process, keeping the general sense 'one contributor among several'.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 factor 指某个尚未命名或新发现的、参与过程的动因，保留“若干促成者之一”的一般含义。

senses.title: Verb: factor in
senses.definition: to include something as one of the elements in a calculation or decision
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物作为计算或决策中的要素纳入考虑
senses.example: We factored in the extra travel time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把额外的路程时间计算在内了。
senses.why: To factor something in is to add it to the set of multipliers before the result is produced.
senses.whyCN: factor something in 就是在结果产生之前，把它加入那组“乘数”里。

senses.title: Verb: factor out
senses.definition: to remove one element from a whole, especially in algebra or analysis
senses.definitionCN: 从整体中分离出一个要素，尤用于代数或分析
senses.example: We can factor out the common term.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以把公因式提取出来。
senses.why: This is the reverse of factoring in: one multiplier is taken out of the product and set beside the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这是 factor in 的逆操作：一个乘数被从乘积中取出，放在其余部分旁边。

senses.title: Commerce: a commission agent
senses.titleCN: 商业：佣金代理人；保理商
senses.definition: a person or firm that buys and sells goods for another, or buys receivables at a discount
senses.definitionCN: 为他人买卖货物的个人或商行，或折价买入应收账款的机构
senses.example: The factor advanced cash against the invoices.
senses.exampleCN: 保理商按发票垫付了现金。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from the early 15th century: Latin factor 'doer, maker' became 'one who does business for another'. Factoring is still the name of the finance practice.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，始于 15 世纪初：拉丁语 factor“做事者、制造者”变成“替他人做买卖的人”。factoring 至今仍是这种金融业务的名字。

senses.title: Genetics: an inherited determinant
senses.definition: a gene or inherited element that determines a trait
senses.definitionCN: 决定某一性状的基因或遗传要素
senses.example: Researchers identified a factor linked to the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者发现了一个与该疾病相关的遗传因子。
senses.why: Early genetics called genes 'factors' because they were unseen units whose effects combined, exactly the mathematical image of multiplying contributions.
senses.whyCN: 早期遗传学把基因称为 factor，因为它们是看不见的单位，其效应会组合起来，正是“多个贡献相乘”的数学意象。

intro.en: Factor is a Latin agent noun from facere 'to do, make'. The commercial sense came first, then the mathematical, then the everyday sense of a contributing element.
intro.cn: factor 是来自 facere“做、制造”的拉丁施动名词。商业义先出现，然后是数学义，最后才是日常的“促成要素”义。

items.en: First recorded as 'commercial agent, deputy, one who buys or sells for another', from French facteur 'agent, representative'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“商业代理人、代表、替他人买卖的人”，来自法语 facteur“代理人、代表”。

items.en: Latin factor 'doer, maker, performer', in Medieval Latin 'agent', is an agent noun from the past-participle stem of facere 'to do, make'. Facere descends from PIE *dhe- 'to set, put'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 factor“做事者、制造者、执行者”，中世纪拉丁语中为“代理人”，是 facere“做、制造”过去分词词干的施动名词。facere 源自原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置”。

items.en: The mathematical sense appears: 'the quantities given to be multiplied one by the other are called factors'.
items.cn: 数学义出现：“被彼此相乘的那些量称为 factors”。

items.en: The sense 'circumstance producing a result' is attested, derived from the mathematical sense by analogy of multiplying contributions.
items.cn: “产生结果的情况”这一义项有记录，是由数学义通过“各贡献相乘”的类比衍生而来。

items.en: The word now spans commerce (factoring), mathematics (factorize), biology (growth factor) and ordinary decisions (a key factor).
items.cn: 现代英语中它横跨商业（保理）、数学（因式分解）、生物学（生长因子）和日常决策（关键因素）。

note.en: Look-alikes are separated by their Latin verbs, near meanings by whether they name a cause, a part, or a measurement.
note.cn: 形近词按拉丁动词区分，近义词按它们指原因、部分还是量度区分。

entries.definition: a building where goods are made. It comes from factor in the old sense of a person managing production, plus -y 'place of'.
entries.definitionCN: 制造货物的场所。它来自 factor 旧义“管理生产的人”，加 -y“场所”。

entries.definition: something that is true or has happened. It is from Latin factum 'a thing done', a sibling of factor.
entries.definitionCN: 真实或已发生的事。它来自拉丁语 factum“做过的事”，与 factor 同根。

entries.definition: a small organized group within a larger one. It comes from facere too, but means 'a acting together', not a multiplier.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部的小派系。它也来自 facere，但意思是“一起行动的一群人”，不是乘数。

entries.definition: the product of all whole numbers up to a given number, written n!. It is formed from factor + -ial.
entries.definitionCN: 从 1 到某整数的所有整数之积，写作 n!。它由 factor + -ial 构成。

entries.definition: one part of a whole. It stresses membership in a structure, while factor stresses contribution to a result.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一个部分。它强调属于某个结构，而 factor 强调对结果的促成作用。

entries.definition: the reason something happens. A cause is stronger and more direct than a factor, which may be only one of several influences.
entries.definitionCN: 事情发生的原因。cause 比 factor 更强、更直接，而 factor 可能只是若干影响之一。

entries.definition: a part of a machine or system. It is physical or structural, not a contributor in a calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 机器或系统的部件。它偏物理或结构，不是计算中的促成量。

entries.definition: a quantity that can change in an experiment. It matches factor in research contexts but implies measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 实验中可变化的量。它在研究语境中与 factor 对应，但暗含“可测量”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin facere family and the real modern compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁 facere 词族和真实的现代复合词。

normal.en: Factor is 'the doer': Latin facere 'do' gives factor, fact, factory and faction.
normal.cn: factor 是“做事者”：拉丁语 facere“做”产生 factor、fact、factory、faction。

normal.en: In maths, factors multiply to make a product; in life, factors combine to make an outcome.
normal.cn: 数学中因数是相乘得到积的数；生活中因素组合起来产生结果。

normal.en: Factor in means add one more multiplier; factor out means take one away.
normal.cn: factor in 是再加一个乘数；factor out 是拿走一个。

normal.en: A risk factor is a condition that raises the chance of a bad result.
normal.cn: risk factor 是提高坏结果发生概率的条件。

normal.en: Factoring is the finance practice where a factor buys invoices at a discount.
normal.cn: factoring 是保理业务：由 factor 折价买入发票。

abstract.en: Picture several hands pushing the same box: each hand is a factor, and the box moves as their combined result.
abstract.cn: 想象好几只手推同一个箱子：每只手都是一个 factor，箱子在合力下移动。

abstract.en: Picture a multiplication table: each number is a factor, and the product appears where they meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张乘法表：每个数都是 factor，乘积出现在它们相交的格子里。

abstract.en: Picture one hand removed from the box: factoring out is that removal, leaving the other hands visible.
abstract.cn: 想象从箱子上拿走一只手：factor out 就是这次移除，让其余的手显露出来。

examples.en: Price is only one factor; reliability matters just as much.
examples.cn: 价格只是一个因素，可靠性同样重要。

examples.en: The model factors in population growth and migration.
examples.cn: 该模型把人口增长和迁移计算在内。

examples.en: The error grew by a factor of five after the update.
examples.cn: 更新之后误差增大了五倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: “罚克特”——被罚的人、被克扣的人，都是影响结果的因素 → factor 因素

root: 拉丁 facere“做、制造”的施动名词 factor“做事者”，由“做事的人”引申为“起作用的东西、因素”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of factor all keep one idea: a unit that combines with others to produce something. The units can be numbers, conditions, genes, or business agents.
sensesIntro.cn: factor 的八个义项都保留一个观念：与其他单位组合以产生某物的单位。这些单位可以是数字、条件、基因，也可以是商人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several separate forces act together, and the result is their product.
core.cn: 核心意象：几种分开的力量共同作用，结果就是它们的乘积。

branches.en: CONTRIBUTORS: a circumstance, a biological agent, or a gene each adds its share to an outcome.
branches.cn: 促成者：一种情况、一种生物因子或一个基因，各自为结果贡献一份力量。

branches.en: NUMBERS: a divisor builds a product, and a multiplier tells how many times one quantity is scaled.
branches.cn: 数字：因数构成乘积，倍数说明一个量被缩放多少倍。

branches.en: VERB: factoring in adds a unit to the account before the decision is made.
branches.cn: 动词：factor in 是把一个单位先计入账内，再作决定。

branches.en: COMMERCE: the oldest sense, where a factor is a person who does business for another.
branches.cn: 商业：最古老的义项，factor 是替他人做生意的人。

branches.en: ALGEBRA: the visible case where a common multiplier is lifted out of an expression.
branches.cn: 代数：最直观的情形，把公因式从表达式中提出来。

intro.en: Factor is a ready-made Latin agent noun in -or. English builds -ial, -ize, -ization, and the business noun factoring.
intro.cn: factor 是现成的拉丁施动名词，后缀 -or。英语在此基础上构成 -ial、-ize、-ization，以及商业名词 factoring。

latinIntro.en: The facere family is one of the largest in Latin: facere, factum, factor, factio, effectus, perfectus, and the frequentative factitare. English keeps it in fact, factory, faction, feature and difficult.
latinIntro.cn: facere 词族是拉丁语中最大的词族之一：facere、factum、factor、factio、effectus、perfectus，以及反复动词 factitare。英语把它保留在 fact、factory、faction、feature、difficult 中。

items.meaning: a doer; one element that produces a result
items.meaningCN: 做事者；产生结果的一个要素（fac-“做”+ -or 施动名词）
items.example: Trust was a key factor in the deal.
items.exampleCN: 信任是这笔交易的关键因素。

items.meaning: the product of all whole numbers up to n
items.meaningCN: 阶乘；阶乘的（factor + -ial）
items.example: Five factorial is one hundred and twenty.
items.exampleCN: 5 的阶乘是 120。

items.meaning: to break a number or expression into factors
items.meaningCN: 因式分解；把……分解为因数（-ize 表示“使成为”）
items.example: Factorize the expression completely.
items.exampleCN: 把这个表达式彻底因式分解。

items.meaning: the act or result of breaking into factors
items.meaningCN: 因式分解（-ation 构成动作名词）
items.example: Prime factorization is unique for each number.
items.exampleCN: 每个数的质因数分解都是唯一的。

items.meaning: depending on several factors
items.meaningCN: 多因素的（multi-“多”+ factor + -ial）
items.example: The disease is multifactorial.
items.exampleCN: 这种疾病由多种因素造成。

items.meaning: the business of buying receivables at a discount
items.meaningCN: 保理业务；应收款转让（-ing 构成名词）
items.example: The company used factoring to raise cash.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司用保理业务筹集现金。

items.meaning: a building where goods are manufactured
items.meaningCN: 工厂（-y 表示场所）
items.example: The old factory is now a museum.
items.exampleCN: 那座老工厂现在是博物馆。

items.meaning: something that is true or has occurred
items.meaningCN: 事实；已发生的事（拉丁 factum“做过的事”）
items.example: The fact is that the plan failed.
items.exampleCN: 事实是这个计划失败了。

items.meaning: a small group acting together within a larger body
items.meaningCN: 派系；小集团（-tion 构成名词）
items.example: The party split into rival factions.
items.exampleCN: 该党分裂成对立的派系。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 做；制造；完成（factor、fact、factory 的共同词根）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：他做一件作品。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 做事者；制造者；执行者（英语 factor 的直接来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：这项工作的执行者。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 做过的事；行为（英语 fact 的来源）

latinEntries.meaning: a making; a party or faction
latinEntries.meaningCN: 制作；派别（英语 faction 的来源）

definition_zh: 特征；特色；五官；专题报道；以……为特色
definition_en: a distinctive part or quality of something, or to give special prominence to someone or something
core_image: 一张脸上被描出的线条：让事物可被认出的部分
scene: 发布会大屏上，折叠手机和三摄模组的参数图逐页切换。 On the big screen the presenter showed the folding screen, the three cameras, and the all-day battery — the key features of the new phone.
sceneCN: 这里 feature 是「特色功能、卖点」（第 1 个义项：使事物有辨识度的显著部分）；句意：主持人在大屏上展示折叠屏、三摄和全天续航，这些是新机的关键特色。

pos.zh: 特征；特色；容貌（features）；专题报道
以……为特色；由……主演；突出展示
起重要作用；占显著位置（feature in）

derivatives.zh: 被特别展示的；作为主角的

senses.title: A distinctive part or quality
senses.definition: an important or noticeable part of something that helps identify it
senses.definitionCN: 某物重要或显眼的部分，有助于识别它
senses.example: The app's best feature is its offline mode.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用最好的特色是离线模式。
senses.why: The word began in late 14c. as 'make, bodily form, fashion' and by the 1690s meant any distinctive part. A feature is what makes a thing recognizable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 14 世纪晚期起初表示“构造、形体、样式”，到 17 世纪 90 年代指任何显著部分。feature 就是让事物可被认出的东西。

senses.title: The face: features as the five facial features
senses.definition: in the plural, the parts of the face and their shape
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指面部的各部分及其轮廓
senses.example: She has strong, angular features.
senses.exampleCN: 她的五官轮廓分明、棱角清晰。
senses.why: This is the oldest surviving sense: Latin factura 'a formation' became Old French faiture 'shape, countenance'. The face is the first 'formed' thing we notice.
senses.whyCN: 这是保留下来最古老的义项：拉丁语 factura“成形”变成古法语 faiture“形状、面容”。脸是我们最先注意到的“被塑造”之物。

senses.title: Media: a special article or program
senses.titleCN: 媒体：专题报道或特别节目
senses.definition: a long article, broadcast, or section devoted to one subject
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某一主题的长篇文章、广播节目或板块
senses.example: The magazine ran a feature on the new museum.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志做了一篇关于新博物馆的专题报道。
senses.why: Journalism adopted the word by 1855, and entertainment by 1801: the subject is given special prominence, made the 'distinctive part' of the issue.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业在 1855 年、娱乐业在 1801 年采用此词：主题被特别突出，成为这一期的“显著部分”。

senses.title: Film: the main attraction
senses.definition: the main film in a cinema program, as opposed to a short
senses.definitionCN: 影院节目中的主片，相对于短片而言
senses.example: The feature starts after two trailers.
senses.exampleCN: 正片在两支预告片之后开始。
senses.why: By 1913 'feature' meant the full-length film that carries the program. It is the main distinctive item, with shorts as the support.
senses.whyCN: 到 1913 年，feature 指撑起整场节目的长片。它是主要的、有辨识度的项目，短片只是陪衬。

senses.title: Verb: include as a highlight
senses.definition: to include someone or something as an important part of a product or event
senses.definitionCN: 把某人某物作为产品或活动的重要部分纳入
senses.example: The new phone features a larger battery.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新手机以更大的电池为特色。
senses.why: The verb appears in 1888 with the sense 'make special display or attraction of'. The noun's 'distinctive part' becomes an action: to put that part forward.
senses.whyCN: 动词在 1888 年出现，义为“特别展示、作为吸引力”。名词“显著部分”变成动作：把那个部分推到前面。

senses.title: Verb: play a prominent part
senses.titleCN: 动词：占显著位置、起重要作用
senses.definition: to be a noticeable or important element in something
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事物中显眼或重要的元素
senses.example: Cost concerns featured heavily in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 成本问题在辩论中占了很大分量。
senses.why: Here the subject is the element that stands out. The same prominence is seen from the other side: instead of the whole featuring a part, the part features in the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这里主语是那个突出的元素。同一种“显著”从另一面看：不是整体突出某个部分，而是该部分在整体中突出。

senses.title: Linguistics: a distinctive property
senses.definition: a property used to distinguish one sound, word, or category from another
senses.definitionCN: 用来区分一个语音、词或类别的属性
senses.example: Voicing is a feature that separates /b/ from /p/.
senses.exampleCN: 浊音是区分 /b/ 与 /p/ 的一个特征。
senses.why: Linguistics turns 'distinctive part' into a technical unit: the smallest property that makes two items different.
senses.whyCN: 语言学把“显著部分”变成技术单位：使两个项目产生差异的最小属性。

senses.title: Geography: a landform
senses.definition: a noticeable physical part of a landscape, such as a hill, lake, or cliff
senses.definitionCN: 地貌中显眼的自然部分，如山丘、湖泊或悬崖
senses.example: The waterfall is the area's most famous natural feature.
senses.exampleCN: 瀑布是该地区最著名的自然景观。
senses.why: Maps and geography use the word for anything on the surface that stands out and can be named.
senses.whyCN: 地图学和地理学用它指地表上任何突出且可命名的东西。

intro.en: Feature goes back to Latin factura 'a formation', from facere 'to make'. English borrowed it through Old French faiture, and the sense moved from 'shape' to 'distinctive part'.
intro.cn: feature 可追溯到拉丁语 factura“成形”，来自 facere“制造”。英语经古法语 faiture 借入，词义从“形状”发展为“显著部分”。

items.en: Recorded as feture, 'make, bodily form, fashion', also 'lines or other characteristics of the face', from Anglo-French feture.
items.cn: 记录为 feture，义为“构造、形体、样式”，也指“面部线条或其他特征”，来自盎格鲁法语 feture。

items.en: Old French faiture 'deed, action; fashion, shape, form; countenance' descends from Latin factura 'a formation, a working'.
items.cn: 古法语 faiture“行为、行动；样式、形状、形体；面容”来自拉丁语 factura“成形、制作”。

items.en: Factura is from the past-participle stem of facere 'make, do, perform', from PIE *dhe- 'to set, put'. The same Latin noun also gives Spanish hechura, Portuguese feitura and Italian fattura.
items.cn: factura 来自 facere“制造、做、完成”的过去分词词干，源自原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置”。同一个拉丁名词还产生西班牙语 hechura、葡萄牙语 feitura、意大利语 fattura。

items.en: The sense 'distinctive part of anything' is established. Entertainment use follows in 1801, journalism in 1855, and 'feature film' in 1913.
items.cn: “任何事物的显著部分”这一义项确立。娱乐义随后见于 1801 年，新闻义见于 1855 年，“故事片”义见于 1913 年。

items.en: The family includes featureless, featurette and featured. Note that feature and factor are cousins: both descend from facere, but through different Latin nouns.
items.cn: 词族包括 featureless、featurette、featured。要注意 feature 与 factor 是表亲：都源自 facere，但经由不同的拉丁名词。

note.en: Look-alikes are separated by the facere family and by sound; near meanings by whether the item is a quality, a part, or a prominent element.
note.cn: 形近词按 facere 词族和读音区分；近义词按所指的是性质、部件还是突出元素区分。

entries.definition: an element that contributes to a result. It is a cousin from Latin factor 'doer', not a form of feature.
entries.definitionCN: 促成结果的要素。它是来自拉丁语 factor“做事者”的表亲，不是 feature 的变形。

entries.definition: an impressive achievement. It comes from Latin factum 'thing done', and is unrelated in sense to feature.
entries.definitionCN: 了不起的成就。它来自拉丁语 factum“做过的事”，与 feature 词义无关。

entries.definition: having no distinctive features; bland. It is feature + -less.
entries.definitionCN: 没有显著特征的；平淡的。它是 feature + -less。

entries.definition: the present participle, used to introduce a featured performer or element. It is not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，用来引出被突出展示的表演者或元素。它不是独立单词。

entries.definition: a quality that typifies a person or thing. It is more abstract than feature, which can also be a physical part.
entries.definitionCN: 典型地体现某人某物的性质。它比 feature 更抽象，因为 feature 也可以指身体部位。

entries.definition: a particular quality in a person's character. It is mostly used for people and living things.
entries.definitionCN: 人性格中的特定品质。它主要用于人和生物。

entries.definition: a quality or property belonging to someone or something. It is formal and often analytical.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某人某物的性质或属性。它较正式，常用于分析。

entries.definition: one side or view of a situation. It is a way of looking at a whole, while a feature is a part that stands out.
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个侧面或视角。它是对整体的看法，而 feature 是突出的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin factura / facere connection and the real modern media senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁 factura / facere 联系，以及真实的现代媒体义项。

normal.en: Feature and factory are cousins through facere: a factory makes things, and a feature is a made, formed part of a thing.
normal.cn: feature 与 factory 经 facere 成为表亲：工厂制造东西，feature 是事物被“塑造”出的部分。

normal.en: Latin factura 'formation' became Old French faiture 'shape, face', which is why features can mean the facial features.
normal.cn: 拉丁 factura“成形”变成古法语 faiture“形状、面容”，所以 features 可以指五官。

normal.en: A feature film is the main, full-length item, the one the program is built around.
normal.cn: feature film 是主要的全长影片，是整场节目围绕的那一项。

normal.en: A feature article gives one subject special prominence in a magazine.
normal.cn: feature article 让某一主题在杂志中获得特别突出的位置。

normal.en: The verb features means 'puts forward as a highlight', as a phone features a large battery.
normal.cn: 动词 feature 意为“作为亮点推出”，如手机以更大的电池为特色。

abstract.en: Picture a face drawn with a few strong lines: those lines are its features, the parts that make it recognizable.
abstract.cn: 想象用几根有力的线条画出一张脸：这些线条就是它的 features，是让脸可被认出的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a product on a lit stage: the spotlight picks out one part, and that lit part is the feature.
abstract.cn: 想象产品放在打光的舞台上：聚光灯挑出一个部分，被照亮的那个部分就是 feature。

abstract.en: Picture a magazine opened to a long article: the article is given the center spread, so it features that subject.
abstract.cn: 想象杂志翻到一篇长文：文章占据跨页中心，于是它把那个主题“作为特色”呈现出来。

examples.en: The most useful feature of the tool is that it works offline.
examples.cn: 这个工具最有用的特色是离线也能工作。

examples.en: Her face has the fine features of her grandmother.
examples.cn: 她的脸有着祖母那样清秀的五官。

examples.en: The exhibition features works by local artists.
examples.cn: 展览以本地艺术家的作品为特色。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肥车子”——一辆很肥的车子，最显眼的是它的外形特征 → feature 特征、特色

root: 拉丁 facere“制造、成形”→ factura“成形之物”，经古法语 faiture 进入英语，核心是“被塑造出的显著部分”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of feature all point to a part that makes a whole recognizable. The part may be a quality, a facial line, a media item, or a landform.
sensesIntro.cn: feature 的八个义项都指向“让整体可被认出的部分”。这个部分可以是性质、面部线条、媒体作品，也可以是地形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: certain lines or parts stand out from the rest and make the whole identifiable.
core.cn: 核心意象：某些线条或部分从其余部分中凸显出来，使整体可被识别。

branches.en: DISTINCTIVE PARTS: a quality, a linguistic property, and a landform are each a marked part of a larger whole.
branches.cn: 显著部分：性质、语言学属性、地形，各自都是更大整体中的标记性部分。

branches.en: THE FACE: the earliest sense, where the 'formed' surface is a person's countenance.
branches.cn: 面容：最早的义项，“被塑造”的表面就是人的面容。

branches.en: MEDIA: a special article or the main film is the item given prominence in a program.
branches.cn: 媒体：专题文章或主片，是节目中被突出呈现的那一项。

branches.en: TO HIGHLIGHT: the verb puts the distinctive part forward on purpose.
branches.cn: 突出展示：动词有意把显著部分推到前面。

branches.en: TO STAND OUT: the same prominence seen from the part's side, as when costs feature in a debate.
branches.cn: 占据显著位置：从部分这一侧看同一种突出，如成本在辩论中占重要位置。

intro.en: Feature is a French-shaped descendant of Latin factura. English adds -less, -ed, -ing and the diminutive -ette, and compounds with film.
intro.cn: feature 是拉丁 factura 的法国化后裔。英语加 -less、-ed、-ing 和指小后缀 -ette，并与 film 构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The facere family includes factura, factor, factum and factio. Feature reaches factura through French; factor reaches factor directly from Latin, so the two are cousins, not derivatives of each other.
latinIntro.cn: facere 词族包括 factura、factor、factum、factio。feature 经法语到达 factura；factor 直接从拉丁语来，因此两者是表亲，不是彼此的派生词。

items.meaning: a distinctive part; to give prominence to
items.meaningCN: 特征；以……为特色（古法语 faiture < 拉丁 factura“成形”）
items.example: The garden's best feature is the old wall.
items.exampleCN: 花园最好的特色是那堵老墙。

items.meaning: the parts of the face
items.meaningCN: 五官；面部特征（复数形式）
items.example: His features are sharp and regular.
items.exampleCN: 他的五官轮廓分明而端正。

items.meaning: without distinctive features
items.meaningCN: 无特征的；平淡无奇的（-less 表示“没有”）
items.example: A featureless concrete wall blocked the view.
items.exampleCN: 一堵毫无特色的混凝土墙挡住了视线。

items.meaning: given special prominence; included as a main item
items.meaningCN: 被特别展示的；作为主角的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The featured artist opened the show.
items.exampleCN: 被重点推介的艺术家为演出开场。

items.meaning: including as a featured performer or element
items.meaningCN: 由……主演；以……为特色（-ing 分词）
items.example: A new album featuring three singers.
items.exampleCN: 一张由三位歌手参与的新专辑。

items.meaning: a short documentary or film
items.meaningCN: 短纪录片；短片（-ette 指小）
items.example: The DVD includes a behind-the-scenes featurette.
items.exampleCN: DVD 收录了一段幕后短片。

items.meaning: the main full-length film on a program
items.meaningCN: 故事片；正片（复合词）
items.example: The festival opened with a feature film.
items.exampleCN: 电影节以一部故事片开幕。

items.meaning: long enough to be a main film
items.meaningCN: 达到正片长度的（复合形容词）
items.example: The documentary is feature-length.
items.exampleCN: 这部纪录片达到正片长度。

items.meaning: to mar or deface; a rare literary verb
items.meaningCN: 损毁外貌；使变形（罕见文学动词，dis- 表示“反、去除”）
items.example: Time had disfeatured the statue.
items.exampleCN: 时间损毁了雕像的外貌。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 制造；做；完成（factura、factor 的共同词根）

latinEntries.meaning: a formation, a working, a making
latinEntries.meaningCN: 成形；制作；制造物（英语 feature 的拉丁来源）
做过的事；行为（英语 fact 的来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：值得纪念的行为。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 做事者；制造者（英语 factor 的直接来源，与 feature 同根）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：万事的促成者。

definition_zh: 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的
definition_en: relating to a union of states or to the central government of such a union
core_image: 各州把手握在一起，同时保留各自的手
scene: 国会大厦前，投票机旁立着州旗与国旗。 Federal law in the United States requires every state to provide accessible voting machines on election day.
sceneCN: 这里 federal 是「联邦层面的、联邦政府的」（第 2 个义项：美国联邦政府的事务）；句意：美国联邦法律要求各州在选举日提供无障碍投票设备。

pos.zh: （历史）联邦派；北方联邦军士兵

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 在联邦层面；由联邦政府

senses.title: Based on a federal union
senses.definition: relating to a system in which separate states share one central authority
senses.definitionCN: 与各独立州共享一个中央权力的制度有关
senses.example: Canada is a federal state with ten provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 加拿大是由十个省组成的联邦制国家。
senses.why: Latin foedus means 'covenant, league, treaty'. A federal system is one formed by an agreement among independent parts, not by one part swallowing the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 foedus 意为“盟约、联盟、条约”。联邦制是由独立部分通过协议形成的制度，而不是一个部分吞并其余部分。

senses.title: US: the national government
senses.definition: belonging to the central government of the United States rather than to a state
senses.definitionCN: 属于美国中央政府，而非某一个州
senses.example: Federal law overrides state law in this area.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一领域，联邦法律优先于州法律。
senses.why: After 1787 the American usage split the single word into levels: state governments and the federal government above them. The adjective became the everyday label for the upper level.
senses.whyCN: 1787 年之后，美国用法把同一个词分成层级：州政府与位于其上的联邦政府。这个形容词成了上一层的日常标签。

senses.title: National rather than regional
senses.definition: in federal states such as Australia or Germany, belonging to the national level
senses.definitionCN: 在澳大利亚、德国等联邦制国家中，属于国家层面
senses.example: The federal parliament met in Canberra.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦议会在堪培拉召开。
senses.why: The same inside/outside logic applies: the federal level stands above the state or provincial level, and the word marks that higher tier.
senses.whyCN: 同样的内外逻辑在这里适用：联邦层面位于州或省层面之上，这个词标记的就是这个更高的层级。

senses.title: Historical: the Union side
senses.titleCN: 历史：美国内战的联邦一方
senses.definition: in the American Civil War, belonging to the Northern forces
senses.definitionCN: 在美国内战中，属于北方联邦军一方
senses.example: Federal troops occupied the city in 1862.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年联邦军队占领了这座城市。
senses.why: From 1861 the word was used for the Northern forces, because they claimed to represent the federal union against the seceding states.
senses.whyCN: 从 1861 年起，这个词用于指北方军队，因为他们声称代表联邦联合，对抗脱离的南方各州。

senses.title: Institutional: federal court or agency
senses.titleCN: 机构层面：联邦法院或联邦机构
senses.definition: used in the names of national courts, agencies, and departments
senses.definitionCN: 用于国家法院、机构和部门的名称
senses.example: The case was moved to a federal court.
senses.exampleCN: 案件被移送至联邦法院。
senses.why: An institution is federal when it belongs to the central level and has authority across state lines.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构属于中央层面并拥有跨州权威时，它就是 federal。

senses.title: Legal authority over the whole union
senses.titleCN: 覆盖整个联邦的法律权威
senses.definition: having legal force across all member states of the union
senses.definitionCN: 在联邦所有成员州都具有法律效力
senses.example: Federal regulations apply in every state.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦法规适用于每一个州。
senses.why: The covenant that creates the union also creates a level of law that sits above the separate parts.
senses.whyCN: 缔造联邦的盟约也创造了一个高于各独立部分的法律层级。

senses.title: Fiscal: federal funding and tax
senses.titleCN: 财政：联邦拨款与联邦税
senses.definition: relating to money raised and spent by the central government
senses.definitionCN: 与中央政府征收和支出的钱有关
senses.example: The project relies on federal funding.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目依赖联邦拨款。
senses.why: Money follows authority: a government that can tax and spend across the union is described by the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 钱跟着权力走：能在整个联邦征税和支出的政府，也用同一个形容词来描述。

senses.title: A union of separate units
senses.titleCN: 由独立单位组成的联合体
senses.definition: describing a union in which the parts keep their own identity, as in 'a federal Europe'
senses.definitionCN: 描述各部分保留自身身份的联合，如“联邦制的欧洲”
senses.example: Some argue for a federal Europe with strong regions.
senses.exampleCN: 有人主张建立一个拥有强大地区的联邦欧洲。
senses.why: This is the word's broadest political sense: unity at the top, separate identities below, all resting on a covenant.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最宽泛的政治义：上层统一、下层保留各自身份，整体建立在盟约之上。

intro.en: Federal comes from Latin foedus 'covenant, league'. It began as a theological word about covenants, then became political in the 17th and 18th centuries.
intro.cn: federal 来自拉丁语 foedus“盟约、联盟”。它最初是讨论“约”的神学术语，17 至 18 世纪才转为政治用语。

items.en: First recorded as a theological term referring to covenants between God and man, from French fédéral.
items.cn: 最早记录为神学术语，指上帝与人之间的“约”，来自法语 fédéral。

items.en: From Latin foedus (genitive foederis) 'covenant, league, treaty, alliance', from PIE *bhoid-es-, a suffixed form of root *bheidh- 'to trust, confide, persuade'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 foedus（属格 foederis）“盟约、联盟、条约、同盟”，源自原始印欧语 *bhoid-es-，是词根 *bheidh-“信任、托付、说服”的加缀形式。

items.en: The secular sense 'pertaining to a covenant or treaty' leads to the political sense 'formed by agreement among independent states' (1707), popularized in federal union during the formation of the United States.
items.cn: 世俗义“与盟约或条约有关的”发展为政治义“由独立国家协议组成”（1707 年），并在美国建国期间的 federal union 一语中流行开来。

items.en: The sense 'favouring the central government' appears, alongside the use of federal (as opposed to confederate) for a state whose central authority is independent within its sphere.
items.cn: “支持中央政府”的义项出现，同时 federal（与 confederate 相对）用来指中央权威在其权限内独立于组成部分的国家。

items.en: Used for the Northern forces in the American Civil War, and later for national courts, agencies and budgets.
items.cn: 1861 年起用于美国内战的北方军队，后来用于国家法院、机构和预算。

note.en: Look-alikes all belong to the foedus family, so the key is what kind of union each names; near meanings differ in whether the centre or the parts are emphasized.
note.cn: 形近词都属于 foedus 词族，关键是各自指哪种联合；近义词则在于强调中心还是强调组成部分。

entries.definition: a union of states or organizations. It is the noun for the thing federal describes.
entries.definitionCN: 州或组织的联合体。它是 federal 所描述之物的名词形式。

entries.definition: to join separate units into a federation. It names the act of forming the covenant.
entries.definitionCN: 使结成联邦。它指形成盟约这一动作。

entries.definition: joined in a loose league where the parts keep most power. It contrasts with federal, where the centre has independent authority.
entries.definitionCN: 结成松散的同盟，各部分保留大部分权力。它与 federal 相对，后者中央拥有独立权威。

entries.definition: a supporter of federal union, or in US history a member of the Federalist Party. It is federal + -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 联邦联合的支持者，或美国历史上的联邦党人。它是 federal + -ist。

entries.definition: relating to a whole nation. It overlaps with federal in the US, but a national government need not be a federation.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个国家有关。在美国语境中它与 federal 重叠，但全国政府不一定实行联邦制。

entries.definition: at the middle or top of a system. It stresses location of power, while federal stresses the covenant structure.
entries.definitionCN: 位于系统的中心或顶端。它强调权力的位置，而 federal 强调盟约结构。

entries.definition: relating to a confederation, where the centre depends on the member states. It is the looser counterpart of federal.
entries.definitionCN: 与邦联有关，中央依赖成员州。它是 federal 的更松散对应词。

entries.definition: a joining together. It is the general idea behind federal, but it does not say how much power the centre holds.
entries.definitionCN: 联合、结合。它是 federal 背后的一般观念，但不说明中央掌握多少权力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin foedus 'covenant' and the real American political history of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁 foedus“盟约”，以及这个词真实的美国政治史。

normal.en: foedus means 'covenant': a federal union is a league held together by an agreement, not by conquest.
normal.cn: foedus 意为“盟约”：联邦联合是靠协议维系的联盟，而不是征服的产物。

normal.en: Federation, federate and federalist all keep the same 'league' idea; only the ending changes the part of speech.
normal.cn: federation、federate、federalist 都保留同一个“联盟”观念，只是词尾改变了词性。

normal.en: In the US, federal means the level above the states: federal law, federal court, federal tax.
normal.cn: 在美国，federal 指州之上的那一层：联邦法律、联邦法院、联邦税。

normal.en: Confederate is the looser cousin: the parts keep more power, while federal gives the centre independent authority.
normal.cn: confederate 是更松散的亲戚：各部分保留更多权力，而 federal 让中央拥有独立权威。

normal.en: The Federalist Papers argued for the stronger central union, which is why federalist entered political language.
normal.cn: 《联邦党人文集》主张更强的中央联合，这就是 federalist 进入政治语言的原因。

abstract.en: Picture several hands gripping one rope: the grip is the covenant, and federal describes the whole arrangement.
abstract.cn: 想象几只手握同一根绳：握持就是盟约，federal 描述的就是这个整体安排。

abstract.en: Picture a building with a shared roof and separate rooms: the roof is the federal level, the rooms are the states.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋共享屋顶、房间独立的建筑：屋顶是联邦层面，房间是各州。

abstract.en: Picture a contract signed by independent towns: each keeps its flag, but all accept one court above them.
abstract.cn: 想象几个独立城镇签署一份契约：各自保留旗帜，但都接受上方的一个法院。

examples.en: Federal and state officials disagreed about the new rule.
examples.cn: 联邦与州官员对这项新规定意见不一。

examples.en: The federal system divides power between the centre and the regions.
examples.cn: 联邦制在中央与地区之间分配权力。

examples.en: A federal grant paid for the bridge repairs.
examples.cn: 一笔联邦拨款支付了桥梁维修费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: “罚得柔”——各州被罚得柔顺了，只好一起签盟约 → federal 联邦的

root: 拉丁 foedus“盟约、联盟”，核心是“由独立部分签约联合”，因此既指联邦制，也指联邦中央。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of federal all rest on one idea: independent parts are bound by a covenant, and a central level acts for the whole.
sensesIntro.cn: federal 的八个义项都建立在一个观念上：独立部分由盟约联结，一个中央层代表整体行事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate states sign one covenant and set a shared authority above them.
core.cn: 核心意象：各州签署同一份盟约，并在它们之上设立共享权威。

branches.en: THE COVENANT: the union itself, where parts keep their identity and the whole holds together by agreement.
branches.cn: 盟约本身：各部分保留身份，整体靠协议维系。

branches.en: THE CENTRAL LEVEL: in the US, Australia, or Germany, federal marks the national tier above states.
branches.cn: 中央层面：在美国、澳大利亚或德国，federal 标记州之上的国家层级。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND LAW: courts, agencies, and regulations belong to the centre and reach across state lines.
branches.cn: 机构与法律：法院、机构、法规属于中央，并跨越州界生效。

branches.en: MONEY: the centre's power to tax and spend follows from its authority over the union.
branches.cn: 财政：中央对整个联邦的权威，带来征税与支出的权力。

branches.en: CIVIL WAR: the Union side claimed to defend the federal covenant against secession.
branches.cn: 内战：联邦一方声称捍卫联邦盟约、反对脱离。

intro.en: Federal is a French/Latin adjective in -al built on foedus. English adds -ly, -ism, -ist, -ize, and the verbs federate and confederate.
intro.cn: federal 是建立在 foedus 上的法语/拉丁语形容词，后缀 -al。英语加 -ly、-ism、-ist、-ize，以及动词 federate、confederate。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin foedus 'covenant', genitive foederis, with the adjective foederalis. The same root gives confoederare 'to unite' and the English confederate.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 foedus“盟约”，属格 foederis，形容词 foederalis。同一词根产生 confoederare“联合”和英语 confederate。

items.meaning: relating to a union of states
items.meaningCN: 联邦的（foedus“盟约”+ -al 构成形容词）
items.example: The federal government owns the land.
items.exampleCN: 联邦政府拥有这片土地。

items.meaning: at the federal level
items.meaningCN: 在联邦层面；由联邦政府（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The clinic is federally funded.
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所受联邦资助。

items.meaning: the doctrine of federal union
items.meaningCN: 联邦主义；联邦制（-ism 表示主义、制度）
items.example: Federalism shares power between levels.
items.exampleCN: 联邦制在层级之间分配权力。

items.meaning: a supporter of federal union; a member of the Federalist Party
items.meaningCN: 联邦主义者；联邦党人（-ist 表示支持者）
items.example: The Federalist Papers defended the Constitution.
items.exampleCN: 《联邦党人文集》为宪法辩护。

items.meaning: a union of states or organizations
items.meaningCN: 联邦；联合会（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The federation has twenty member clubs.
items.exampleCN: 该联合会有二十个成员俱乐部。

items.meaning: to unite into a federation
items.meaningCN: 使结成联邦（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The colonies federated in 1901.
items.exampleCN: 这些殖民地在 1901 年结成联邦。

items.meaning: united in a loose league
items.meaningCN: 结成邦联的；同盟的（con-“一起”+ foeder- + -ate）
items.example: A confederate system keeps the centre weak.
items.exampleCN: 邦联制让中央保持弱势。

items.meaning: to bring under federal control
items.meaningCN: 使联邦化；归联邦管辖（-ize 表示“使成为”）
items.example: The law federalized the inspection system.
items.exampleCN: 该法律使检查制度联邦化。

items.meaning: relating to a confederation
items.meaningCN: 邦联的（con- + feder- + -al）
items.example: A confederal government depends on member states.
items.exampleCN: 邦联政府依赖成员州。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 盟约；联盟；条约（federal 的词基）
盟约的；联盟的（拉丁形容词）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：盟约性的协定。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 联合成联盟（英语 confederate 的来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：各城邦结成同盟。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 信任；诚信（与 foedus 同出一个“信任”词根）

definition_zh: 财政；金融；资金；为……提供资金
definition_en: the management of money, the money available for a purpose, or to provide money for something
core_image: 把一笔账结清：钱的流动与结算
scene: 施工围挡上贴着新校区的效果图，旁边挂着债券凭证的复印件。 Before the new campus broke ground, the school financed the whole project by issuing bonds.
sceneCN: 这里 finance 是「为……提供资金」（第 4 个义项：动词，出资支持某项计划）；句意：新校区动工前，学校通过发行债券为整个工程筹资。

senses.title: Management of money
senses.definition: the activity or study of managing money, credit, and investment
senses.definitionCN: 管理货币、信贷和投资的活动或学问
senses.example: She studied finance at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习金融。
senses.why: The modern sense 'management of money, science of monetary business' is first recorded in 1770. It grew from the older idea of settling what is owed.
senses.whyCN: 现代义“资金管理、货币业务之学”最早记录于 1770 年，由更早的“结清所欠之账”观念发展而来。

senses.title: Money available for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 可用资金：为某用途准备的财源
