senses.definition: the money that a person or organization has available to spend
senses.definitionCN: 个人或组织可用于支出的钱
senses.example: The project cannot start without finance.
senses.exampleCN: 没有资金，这个项目无法启动。
senses.why: Money that settles a debt is, from the other side, the money you must have. The word shifts from the act of payment to the fund that makes payment possible.
senses.whyCN: 用来结清债务的钱，从另一面看就是你必须拥有的钱。词义从“付款行为”转向“使付款得以发生的资金”。

senses.title: Public finances: the state of funds
senses.definition: in the plural, the income, spending, and debt position of a government or company
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指政府或公司的收入、支出与债务状况
senses.example: The country's public finances are under strain.
senses.exampleCN: 该国的公共财政正处于压力之下。
senses.why: The plural finances, recorded from 1730, names the whole set of monetary resources and obligations, not one payment.
senses.whyCN: 复数 finances 记录于 1730 年，指全部货币资源与义务的集合，而不是一笔付款。

senses.title: Verb: provide money for
senses.definition: to supply the money needed for a project, purchase, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 为项目、购买或组织提供所需资金
senses.example: The bank financed the new factory.
senses.exampleCN: 银行为新工厂提供了资金。
senses.why: The verb sense 'to furnish with money' is from 1866. It turns the noun into an action: put the needed funds in place.
senses.whyCN: 动词义“提供资金”始于 1866 年。它把名词变成动作：把所需资金安置到位。

senses.title: Verb: buy on credit
senses.definition: to arrange credit so that a buyer can pay over time
senses.definitionCN: 安排信贷，使买方可以分期付款
senses.example: They financed the car over three years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用三年分期付款买了这辆车。
senses.why: This is providing money in the form of credit: the purchase happens now, and the payment is settled later.
senses.whyCN: 这是以信贷形式提供资金：购买现在发生，付款以后结清。

senses.title: The business of a company
senses.definition: the department or function that manages a company's money
senses.definitionCN: 管理公司资金的部门或职能
senses.example: Send the invoice to the finance department.
senses.exampleCN: 把发票送到财务部。
senses.why: Organizations concentrate money management in one office, so finance becomes the name of that function and its people.
senses.whyCN: 组织把资金管理集中到一个部门，于是 finance 成为该职能及其人员的名称。

senses.title: The industry and discipline
senses.definition: the industry that deals with banking, investment, and credit, or the academic study of it
senses.definitionCN: 涉及银行、投资和信贷的行业，或对它的学术研究
senses.example: He works in finance in the City of London.
senses.exampleCN: 他在伦敦金融城从事金融工作。
senses.why: A body of knowledge and a sector of the economy both take the name of the activity that defines them.
senses.whyCN: 一门知识与一个经济部门，都以定义它们的活动命名。

senses.title: High finance: large-scale money dealing
senses.titleCN: 大额金融：高层资本运作
senses.definition: the phrase high finance, meaning large and complex financial dealings
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语 high finance，指大额而复杂的金融运作
senses.example: The merger was a matter of high finance.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并是一桩高层金融运作。
senses.why: High finance (1884) marks the upper scale of the same activity: deals involving banks, corporations, and very large sums.
senses.whyCN: high finance（1884）标记同一活动的上层规模：涉及银行、企业和巨额资金的交易。

intro.en: Finance begins with the idea of ending a debt. Old French finer 'to end, settle' gave finance, and the sense moved from settlement to money management.
intro.cn: finance 的起点是“结清债务”。古法语 finer“结束、结清”产生 finance，词义从“结算”发展为“资金管理”。

items.en: First recorded as 'an end, settlement, retribution', from Old French finance 'end, ending; pardon, remission; payment, expense; settlement of a debt'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“结束、结算、清偿”，来自古法语 finance“结束、终止；赦免；付款、开支；债务结清”。

items.en: Finance is a noun of action from finer 'to end, settle a dispute or debt', from fin 'end', from Latin finis 'end'. Medieval Latin finis also meant 'a payment in settlement, fine or tax'.
items.cn: finance 是 finer“结束、解决争端或债务”的动作名词，来自 fin“终点”，再来自拉丁语 finis“终点”。中世纪拉丁语 finis 也指“结算付款、罚金或税”。

items.en: French senses are brought in one by one: 'ransom' (mid-15c.), 'taxation' (late 15c.), then the general idea of money matters.
items.cn: 法语诸义逐次进入英语：15 世纪中期“赎金”，15 世纪晚期“征税”，然后是泛指的“钱务”。

items.en: The sense 'management of money, science of monetary business' is first recorded. The plural finances 'pecuniary resources' follows in 1730.
items.cn: “资金管理、货币业务之学”这一义项最早记录于 1770 年。复数 finances“货币资源”在 1730 年出现。

items.en: The verb sense 'to furnish with money' is recorded; 'to manage money' is from 1827. Financial and financier join the family in the 18th and 19th centuries.
items.cn: 动词义“提供资金”记录于 1866 年；“管理钱财”义始于 1827 年。financial 与 financier 在 18、19 世纪加入这个词族。

note.en: Look-alikes are the fine/end family; near meanings differ in whether they name money as a resource, a fund, or a system.
note.cn: 形近词属于 fine/end 词族；近义词的区别在于指资源、基金还是体系。

entries.definition: relating to money and finance. It is finance + -ial, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱和金融有关的。它是 finance + -ial，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a sum paid as a penalty; also 'of high quality'. The penalty sense comes from 'payment in settlement', the same source as finance.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款；也指“优质的”。罚款义来自“结算付款”，与 finance 同源。

entries.definition: to come to an end. It is the direct 'end' word from finis, while finance is the 'settlement' branch.
entries.definitionCN: 结束；完成。它是 finis 的直接“终点”分支，而 finance 是“结算”分支。

entries.definition: a person who manages large sums of money. It is finance + -ier, a French agent ending.
entries.definitionCN: 管理大笔资金的人。它是 finance + -ier，法语施动后缀。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside for a purpose. It is a concrete pool, while finance can mean the whole system or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的留出的一笔钱。它是具体的资金池，而 finance 可指整个体系或活动。

entries.definition: money provided for a project or organization. It is the result of financing, and is often used of public or research money.
entries.definitionCN: 为项目或组织提供的钱。它是融资的结果，常用于公共或科研经费。

entries.definition: the business of banks. It is one part of finance, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 银行业务。它是金融的一部分，而不是全部。

entries.definition: the study of production, consumption, and wealth. It is broader than finance, which focuses on money and credit.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生产、消费与财富的学科。它比 finance 更广，后者聚焦货币与信贷。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real finis 'end' family and the real modern financial compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 finis“终点”词族，以及真实的现代金融复合词。

normal.en: Latin finis means 'end': finance began as the 'ending' of a debt by paying it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 finis 意为“终点”：finance 最初就是通过付款来“结束”一笔债务。

normal.en: Fine, finish and finance share finis: a fine ends a case, a finish ends a task, and finance settles an account.
normal.cn: fine、finish、finance 共享 finis：罚款结束案件，finish 结束任务，finance 结清账目。

normal.en: The finance department is where a company's money is managed and accounts are settled.
normal.cn: finance department 是公司管钱、结账的地方。

normal.en: To finance a project is to supply the money that lets it go forward.
normal.cn: finance a project 就是提供让项目得以推进的资金。

normal.en: High finance is the large-scale end of the same activity, where banks and corporations move big sums.
normal.cn: high finance 是同一活动的大规模一端，银行与企业在其中调动巨额资金。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with one last unpaid line: paying it ends the account, and that ending is finance.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账上还剩最后一笔未付：付清它就结束了这本账，而这次“结束”就是 finance。

abstract.en: Picture water flowing into a reservoir and then out through pipes: the reservoir is the fund, the flow is finance.
abstract.cn: 想象水流入水库再经管道流出：水库是 fund，流动本身是 finance。

abstract.en: Picture a scale balancing coins and goods: finance is the settling that makes the two sides equal.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平称量钱币与货物：finance 就是让两边相等的结算动作。

examples.en: The city's finances improved after the new tax was introduced.
examples.cn: 引入新税后，该市的财政状况有所改善。

examples.en: The loan financed the first year of the research.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款为研究的第一年提供了资金。

examples.en: She keeps her personal finances in a simple spreadsheet.
examples.cn: 她用一个简单的表格管理个人财务。

dict_mnemonic.text: “罚爱难死”——罚款、爱心捐款、难题开支，样样都要钱 → finance 财政、资金

root: 拉丁 finis“终点” → 古法语 finer“结清” → finance，核心是“把账结清”，引申为“资金、财政、金融”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of finance all come from the act of settling an account. Settlement becomes a fund, then a department, then a whole industry.
sensesIntro.cn: finance 的八个义项都来自“结账”这个动作。结算变成资金，再变成部门，最后变成整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a debt is brought to its end by payment, and the money that ends it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一笔债务通过付款走到终点，以及用来结束它的钱。

branches.en: ACTIVITY: managing money grows into a discipline and an industry.
branches.cn: 活动：管理钱财发展成一门学科和一个行业。

branches.en: RESOURCES: the money available, the whole financial position, and the large-scale dealings all name amounts of capital.
branches.cn: 资源：可用资金、整体财务状况、大额交易，都指资本的数量。

branches.en: PROVISION: the verb supplies the money a project or a purchase needs.
branches.cn: 提供：动词指为一个项目或一笔购买提供所需资金。

branches.en: FUNCTION: inside a company, finance is the office that manages the money.
branches.cn: 职能：在公司内部，finance 是管理资金的部门。

branches.en: CREDIT: paying over time is a settlement postponed, which is why financing a car is still finance.
branches.cn: 信贷：分期付款是把结算推后，所以“贷款买车”仍然是 finance。

intro.en: Finance is a French noun of action from finer. English adds -ial, -ially, -ier, -ing, and the prefix re- for refinance.
intro.cn: finance 是来自 finer 的法语动作名词。英语加 -ial、-ially、-ier、-ing，以及前缀 re- 构成 refinance。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis 'end, boundary' is the base; Medieval Latin gave it the sense 'payment in settlement'. The same finis produces final, finish, finite and define.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis“终点、边界”是词基；中世纪拉丁语赋予它“结算付款”之义。同一个 finis 还产生 final、finish、finite、define。

items.meaning: settlement; the management of money
items.meaningCN: 结算；财政；金融（finer“结清”+ -ance 名词后缀）
items.example: Finance is the study of money and credit.
items.exampleCN: 金融是研究货币与信贷的学问。

items.meaning: relating to money matters
items.meaningCN: 财政的；金融的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The company faces financial trouble.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司面临财务困难。

items.meaning: in money terms
items.meaningCN: 在财务上；经济上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The project is financially viable.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上可行。

items.meaning: a person who manages large sums
items.meaningCN: 金融家；财政家（-ier 表示人）
items.example: A financier backed the railway.
items.exampleCN: 一位金融家资助了这条铁路。

items.meaning: the act or arrangement of providing funds
items.meaningCN: 融资；资金筹措（-ing 构成名词）
items.example: The financing took six months to arrange.
items.exampleCN: 融资安排花了六个月。

items.meaning: to replace an existing loan with a new one
items.meaningCN: 再融资；以新贷款替换旧贷款（re-“再次”）
items.example: They refinanced the mortgage at a lower rate.
items.exampleCN: 他们以更低利率为房贷再融资。

items.meaning: the growing role of financial motives in the economy
items.meaningCN: 金融化（金融动机在经济中作用增强的过程）
items.example: Financialization changed how firms are run.
items.exampleCN: 金融化改变了企业的运作方式。

items.meaning: small loans and financial services for poor borrowers
items.meaningCN: 小额信贷；面向贫困借款人的微型金融（micro-“微小”）
items.example: Microfinance supports small village businesses.
items.exampleCN: 小额信贷支持村庄里的小生意。

items.meaning: the twelve-month period used for accounting
items.meaningCN: 财政年度；会计年度（复合名词）
items.example: The budget is set for the next financial year.
items.exampleCN: 预算为下一个财政年度制定。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 终点；界限；边界（finance 的最终词源）
结束；限定；结清（古法语 finer 的来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：他终结了这场诉讼。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 终点的；最后的（英语 final 的来源）
划定界限；定义（英语 define 的来源，与 finance 同根）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：他为事物划定界限。

definition_zh: 灵活的；可弯曲的；可变通的；有弹性的
definition_en: able to bend easily, or able to change to suit new conditions
core_image: 一根能弯而不断的枝条
scene: 桌上摆着日程表和时钟，接送孩子的时间被标了出来。 When the overtime notice came, she kept her schedule flexible and changed the times for picking up her child.
sceneCN: 这里 flexible 是「可变通的、能随机调整的」（第 2 个义项：能适应变化的条件）；句意：遇到临时加班通知，她把日程安排得灵活，调整了接送孩子的时间。

pos.zh: 灵活的；可变通的；适应力强的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Bendable without breaking
senses.definition: able to be bent easily without breaking or losing shape permanently
senses.definitionCN: 容易弯曲而不断裂，也不会永久失去形状
senses.example: The hose is flexible enough to turn corners.
senses.exampleCN: 这根软管足够柔韧，可以拐弯。
senses.why: Latin flexibilis 'that may be bent' comes from flectere 'to bend'. The first sense is purely physical: the object yields to force and then returns.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 flexibilis“可被弯曲的”来自 flectere“弯曲”。第一个义项完全是物理的：物体在受力时屈服，然后恢复。

senses.title: Adaptable to change
senses.definition: able to change in response to new conditions or needs
senses.definitionCN: 能根据新条件或新需要作出改变
senses.example: Our plans must stay flexible.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的计划必须保持灵活。
senses.why: The physical bend becomes a mental and organizational one: a plan that can bend to new facts will not break under them.
senses.whyCN: 物理的弯曲变成心智与组织上的弯曲：能随新事实弯折的计划，不会在事实压力下折断。

senses.title: Willing to compromise
senses.definition: of a person, willing to change position or accept alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 指人愿意改变立场或接受其他方案
senses.example: She was flexible about the meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 她对会议时间很灵活。
senses.why: A person who can bend is easier to work with. The 15th-century sense already included 'mentally or spiritually pliant'.
senses.whyCN: 能弯曲的人更容易合作。15 世纪的义项已经包含“心智或性情上柔顺”。

senses.title: Flexible hours or schedule
senses.definition: of working time, able to be arranged around other needs
senses.definitionCN: 指工作时间可以围绕其他需要安排
senses.example: The job offers flexible hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作提供弹性工时。
senses.why: Time is treated as a bendable frame: the hours can shift without the whole schedule breaking.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作可弯曲的框架：时段可以移动，而整个日程不会断裂。

senses.title: Adjustable rules or policy
senses.definition: designed so that it can be changed to fit different cases
senses.definitionCN: 设计上可以修改以适应不同情况
senses.example: The guidelines are flexible enough for small schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这些指导原则足够灵活，适用于小型学校。
senses.why: A rule that cannot bend either breaks or breaks the case it is applied to; a flexible rule bends to fit.
senses.whyCN: 不能弯曲的规则要么自身断裂，要么压断它所适用的情形；灵活的规则会弯身贴合。

senses.title: Economics: a flexible exchange rate
senses.definition: of a currency or price, allowed to move with market forces
senses.definitionCN: 指货币或价格可随市场力量变动
senses.example: A flexible exchange rate absorbs shocks.
senses.exampleCN: 浮动汇率能吸收冲击。
senses.why: Economics uses the same image: a rate that is fixed is rigid, while a flexible one yields to supply and demand.
senses.whyCN: 经济学使用同一个意象：固定汇率是僵硬的，浮动汇率则对供求让步。

senses.title: Flexible response: a defence doctrine
senses.definition: the military doctrine of responding to attack with a measured, adaptable range of options
senses.definitionCN: 以适度、可调整的多种选项回应攻击的军事学说
senses.example: NATO adopted the strategy of flexible response.
senses.exampleCN: 北约采纳了“灵活反应”战略。
senses.why: A rigid single response would either fail or escalate; a flexible response bends to the scale of the threat.
senses.whyCN: 僵硬的单一回应要么失效，要么升级；灵活反应则随威胁的规模弯曲调整。

senses.title: A supple body
senses.definition: of a body or limb, able to move through a wide range without strain
senses.definitionCN: 指身体或肢体能大幅度活动而不受伤
senses.example: Gymnasts need a flexible back.
senses.exampleCN: 体操运动员需要柔韧的背部。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense applied to the body: muscles and joints bend, and training increases that range.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理义项用在身体上：肌肉和关节会弯曲，训练会增大活动幅度。

intro.en: Flexible is a Latin adjective from flectere 'to bend'. The verb's deeper origin is uncertain, but the Latin layer and the English history are clear.
intro.cn: flexible 是来自 flectere“弯曲”的拉丁形容词。这个动词的更早来源不确定，但拉丁层与英语历史是清楚的。

items.en: First recorded as 'capable of being bent; mentally or spiritually pliant', from Old French flexible or directly from Latin flexibilis.
items.cn: 最早记录为“可弯曲的；心智或性情柔顺的”，来自古法语 flexible，或直接来自拉丁语 flexibilis。

items.en: Latin flexibilis 'that may be bent, pliant, yielding' comes from flex-, the past-participle stem of flectere 'to bend'. Figuratively it already meant 'tractable, inconstant'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 flexibilis“可弯曲的、柔顺的、易屈服的”来自 flex-，即 flectere“弯曲”的过去分词词干。引申义已表示“可管教的、易变的”。

items.en: The deeper origin of flectere is uncertain. Standard references do not agree on a single Proto-Indo-European root, so the deepest layer is source uncertain.
items.cn: flectere 的更早来源不确定。通行资料没有一致认定的单一原始印欧语词根，因此最深层词源标注为来源不确定。

items.en: Flex, a back-formation from flexible, appears in the 1520s. Flexile and flexive competed with flexible but became rare.
items.cn: flex 由 flexible 逆构而成，出现于 16 世纪 20 年代。flexile 与 flexive 曾与 flexible 竞争，后来变得罕见。

items.en: The family expands into flexibility, flexibly, inflexible, flexion and flexitime. The word covers bodies, plans, rules, currencies and military strategy.
items.cn: 词族扩展出 flexibility、flexibly、inflexible、flexion、flexitime。这个词覆盖身体、计划、规则、货币与军事战略。

note.en: Look-alikes share the flectere stem; near meanings differ in whether the yielding is physical, personal, or structural.
note.cn: 形近词共享 flectere 词干；近义词的区别在于“屈服”是物理的、为人的还是结构性的。

entries.definition: the quality of being able to bend or adapt. It is flexible + -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 可弯曲或可适应的性质。它是 flexible + -ity。

entries.definition: to bend, especially a muscle; also to show off. It was formed from flexible in the 1520s.
entries.definitionCN: 弯曲，尤指屈伸肌肉；也指炫耀。它在 16 世纪 20 年代由 flexible 逆构而成。

entries.definition: an automatic physical response. It is re- 'back' + flectere 'bend', a bending back.
entries.definitionCN: 反射动作。它是 re-“向后”+ flectere“弯曲”，即“弯回去”。

entries.definition: not able to bend or adapt. It is in- 'not' + flexible, and is both physical and personal.
entries.definitionCN: 不能弯曲或变通的。它是 in-“不”+ flexible，既可指物理，也可指性格。

entries.definition: easy to bend or shape, especially by hand. It is more physical than flexible and often used of materials or character.
entries.definitionCN: 容易弯曲或塑形，尤指用手。它比 flexible 更物理，常用于材料或性格。

entries.definition: able to adjust to new conditions. It stresses successful adjustment, while flexible stresses the capacity to bend.
entries.definitionCN: 能适应新条件的。它强调成功调整，而 flexible 强调弯曲的能力。

entries.definition: able to stretch and return to its shape. It implies stretching, while flexible implies bending.
entries.definitionCN: 能拉伸并恢复形状的。它暗含“拉伸”，而 flexible 暗含“弯曲”。

entries.definition: moving and bending easily, especially of a body. It is more often used of living movement than of rules.
entries.definitionCN: 活动与弯曲自如，尤指身体。它更常用于生物的活动，而不是规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real flectere family and the real modern compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 flectere 词族和真实的现代复合词。

normal.en: flectere means 'to bend': flexible things bend, reflex actions bend back, and inflexible things cannot bend.
normal.cn: flectere 意为“弯曲”：flexible 的东西能弯，reflex 是弯回去的动作，inflexible 则不能弯。

normal.en: Flexible hours are hours that can bend around your other duties.
normal.cn: 弹性工时可随你其他事务弯折调整。

normal.en: A flexible rule is not weaker: it bends so that it does not break the case it is applied to.
normal.cn: 灵活规则并不更弱：它弯身，以免压断所适用的情形。

normal.en: A flexible exchange rate moves with the market, unlike a fixed peg.
normal.cn: 浮动汇率随市场变动，不同于固定钉住。

normal.en: Gymnasts train flexibility because a supple back can move through a wider range.
normal.cn: 体操运动员训练柔韧性，因为柔韧的背能完成更大范围的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a young branch bent almost double but springing back: that is the physical core of flexible.
abstract.cn: 想象一根嫩枝几乎被弯成两折，却弹回原状：这就是 flexible 的物理核心。

abstract.en: Picture a road that curves around a hill instead of cutting through it: the flexible plan survives the obstacle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绕山而行的路，而不是硬穿山体：灵活的计划绕过了障碍。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening and closing to hold different objects: the same hand adapts, and that is flexibility.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手张开又合拢去握不同的东西：同一只手在适应，这就是灵活性。

examples.en: The schedule is flexible, so choose the time that suits you.
examples.cn: 日程是灵活的，选一个适合你的时间吧。

examples.en: A flexible approach often works better than a rigid rule.
examples.cn: 灵活的做法往往比僵硬的规则更有效。

examples.en: The cable stays flexible even in cold weather.
examples.cn: 这种电缆在寒冷天气里仍然保持柔韧。

dict_mnemonic.text: “弗莱克瑟波”——弗莱克把身子一弯，钻进狭小的座位 → flexible 灵活的、可弯的

root: 拉丁 flectere“弯曲”+ -ibilis“可……的”，核心是“能弯而不断”，引申为“能适应变化”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of flexible all describe the same capacity: to yield under pressure without breaking. The pressure may be physical, personal, institutional, or economic.
sensesIntro.cn: flexible 的八个义项都描述同一种能力：在压力下屈服而不折断。压力可以是物理的、为人的、制度的或经济的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch bends under force and springs back instead of snapping.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝条在受力时弯曲，然后弹回，而不是折断。

branches.en: BODY AND MATERIAL: hoses, cables, joints and backs bend through a range and recover.
branches.cn: 身体与材料：软管、电缆、关节和背部在范围内弯曲并恢复。

branches.en: PLANS AND RULES: a plan or policy bends to new facts instead of breaking against them.
branches.cn: 计划与规则：计划或政策随新事实弯折，而不是与之硬碰而断。

branches.en: PERSON: a person who can shift position is easier to work with and harder to break.
branches.cn: 人：能改变立场的人更容易合作，也更不容易被折断。

branches.en: TIME: working hours bend around other duties without the schedule collapsing.
branches.cn: 时间：工时可围绕其他事务弯折，而日程不致崩塌。

branches.en: ECONOMY AND DEFENCE: rates and responses yield to market forces or to the scale of a threat.
branches.cn: 经济与防务：汇率与回应随市场力量或威胁规模而调整。

intro.en: Flexible is Latin flexibilis, from flectere. English adds -ity and -ly, negates with in-, and builds flex, flexion and flexitime.
intro.cn: flexible 是拉丁语 flexibilis，来自 flectere。英语加 -ity、-ly，用 in- 构成否定，并构造 flex、flexion、flexitime。

latinIntro.en: The flectere family includes flexus 'a bending', flexibilis, flexio and flexor. English reflect, deflect, inflect and genuflect all keep the 'bend' image.
latinIntro.cn: flectere 词族包括 flexus“弯曲”、flexibilis、flexio、flexor。英语 reflect、deflect、inflect、genuflect 都保留“弯”的意象。

items.meaning: able to bend or adapt
items.meaningCN: 可弯曲的；灵活的（flex-“弯”+ -ible“可……的”）
items.example: The material is strong but flexible.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料坚固而柔韧。

items.meaning: the quality of bending or adapting
items.meaningCN: 灵活性；柔韧性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The job requires flexibility.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作需要灵活性。

items.meaning: in a way that can adapt
items.meaningCN: 灵活地；柔韧地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team works flexibly across time zones.
items.exampleCN: 团队跨时区灵活工作。

items.meaning: unable to bend or adapt
items.meaningCN: 不灵活的；僵化的（in-“不”+ flexible）
items.example: The rules are inflexible and outdated.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则僵化而过时。

items.meaning: rigidity of body or policy
items.meaningCN: 僵化；不可弯曲（in- + flexible + -ity）
items.example: His inflexibility cost him the deal.
items.exampleCN: 他的僵化让他失去了这笔交易。

items.meaning: to bend a muscle; to adjust or show off
items.meaningCN: 屈伸；弯曲；炫耀（由 flexible 逆构）
items.example: He flexed his arm to test it.
items.exampleCN: 他屈伸手臂来试试。

items.meaning: the act of bending, especially a joint
items.meaningCN: 弯曲；屈曲，尤指关节（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Flexion of the knee is painful.
items.exampleCN: 膝关节弯曲时会疼。

items.meaning: a muscle that bends a joint
items.meaningCN: 屈肌（使关节弯曲的肌肉，-or 表示施动）
items.example: The flexor muscles tighten.
items.exampleCN: 屈肌收紧。

items.meaning: a system allowing workers to choose their hours
items.meaningCN: 弹性工作时间制（flexible + time 的复合）
items.example: Flexitime helps parents manage school runs.
items.exampleCN: 弹性工时帮助父母安排接送孩子。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 弯曲；使弯曲；转向（flexible 的词根）
可弯曲的；柔顺的（英语 flexible 的直接来源）
弯曲；摆动（英语 flexion 的来源）
弯回；反射（英语 reflect 的来源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：它把光反射回去。

definition_zh: 波动；起伏；变动；来回变化
definition_en: to rise and fall or change irregularly in level, amount, or quality
core_image: 水面一起一伏的波浪线
scene: 菜市场的价格牌早晚各换一次，蔬菜筐旁的箭头一上一下。 Because of supply and demand, vegetable prices fluctuated a lot this week, and the labels changed morning and evening.
sceneCN: 这里 fluctuate 是「上下波动、起伏不定」（第 1 个义项：价格不规则地涨落）；句意：受供需影响，这周蔬菜价格波动很大，标价早晚都在变。

collocations.zh: 在 A 与 B 之间来回变动

derivatives.zh: 波动的；起伏的（医学中也指可移动的）

senses.title: Prices rise and fall
senses.definition: of prices or values, to go up and down repeatedly and irregularly
senses.definitionCN: 指价格或价值反复而不规则地涨落
senses.example: Oil prices fluctuated all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天油价都在波动。
senses.why: Latin fluctuare is 'to move in waves', from fluctus 'a wave'. A price that rises and falls draws the same up-and-down line as a wave.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fluctuare 意为“像波浪一样运动”，来自 fluctus“波浪”。涨落的价格画出的正是波浪一样的上下曲线。

senses.title: Levels vary over time
senses.definition: of a level such as temperature or water, to keep changing within a range
senses.definitionCN: 指温度、水位等水平在一定范围内持续变化
senses.example: The lake level fluctuates with the seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 湖面水位随季节起伏。
senses.why: Water is the literal source of the image, so a level that rises and falls is the most natural application of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 水是这个意象的字面来源，因此水位的升降是这个动词最自然的用法。

senses.title: Numbers swing
senses.definition: of figures such as rates or sales, to change repeatedly in either direction
senses.definitionCN: 指利率、销量等数字反复朝两个方向变化
senses.example: Sales fluctuate from month to month.
senses.exampleCN: 销量逐月波动。
senses.why: A rate or a sales figure is plotted as a line, and a line that keeps swinging looks like a wave.
senses.whyCN: 利率或销量被画成一条线，反复摆动的线看起来就像波浪。

senses.title: Quality or attendance varies
senses.titleCN: 质量或出勤率时好时坏
senses.definition: of a non-numeric quality, to be uneven from one time or case to another
senses.definitionCN: 指非数字性的质量在不同时间或情形下不均衡
senses.example: The quality of the meals fluctuates.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜的质量时好时坏。
senses.why: Anything measured on a scale can be plotted as a wave, even when the scale is subjective, like quality or turnout.
senses.whyCN: 任何按尺度衡量的东西都能画成波浪，即使尺度是主观的，如质量或出席人数。

senses.title: Opinions and moods shift
senses.definition: of feelings or opinions, to change back and forth
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或意见来回改变
senses.example: Public opinion fluctuated during the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 竞选期间公众意见摇摆不定。
senses.why: The wave image moves from water to the mind: feelings rise and fall without settling at one level.
senses.whyCN: 波浪意象从水面移向心智：情绪起起伏伏，不停在某一水平。

senses.title: Fluctuate between two states
senses.definition: to move repeatedly from one condition to another, as in 'fluctuate between hope and fear'
senses.definitionCN: 反复从一种状态转到另一种，如“在希望与恐惧之间摇摆”
senses.example: He fluctuated between hope and despair.
senses.exampleCN: 他在希望与绝望之间摇摆。
senses.why: A wave has a crest and a trough; to fluctuate between two things is to keep moving from one extreme to the other.
senses.whyCN: 波浪有波峰和波谷；在两者之间 fluctuate，就是在两个极端之间不断移动。

senses.title: Move like a wave
senses.definition: in literary or technical use, to move in a wavelike way
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或技术用法中，像波浪一样运动
senses.example: The surface of the pool fluctuated in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 池面在风中起伏。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense, now rarer in English but still present in technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是原本的物理义项，现代英语中较少见，但仍存在于技术写作中。

senses.title: Economic activity varies
senses.definition: of an economy, currency, or market, to expand and contract irregularly
senses.definitionCN: 指经济、货币或市场不规则地扩张与收缩
senses.example: The currency fluctuated against the dollar.
senses.exampleCN: 该货币对美元的汇率起伏不定。
senses.why: Markets are described as waves in economics, so the verb naturally covers currencies and activity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把市场描述为波浪，因此这个动词自然覆盖货币与经济活动。

intro.en: Fluctuate is a Latin verb built on fluctus 'a wave', from fluere 'to flow'. The etymology is clear and the 'wave' image is the key to every sense.
intro.cn: fluctuate 是建立在 fluctus“波浪”之上的拉丁动词，来自 fluere“流动”。词源清楚，“波浪”意象是理解所有义项的关键。

items.en: First recorded in English, from Latin fluctuatus, past participle of fluctuare 'to undulate, move in waves'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 17 世纪 30 年代，来自拉丁语 fluctuatus，即 fluctuare“起伏、像波浪般运动”的过去分词。

items.en: Fluctuare is from fluctus 'a wave, billow, surge, a flowing', which comes from the past-participle stem of fluere 'to flow'.
items.cn: fluctuare 来自 fluctus“波浪、巨浪、涌动、流动”，后者来自 fluere“流动”的过去分词词干。

items.en: Fluere comes from an extended form of PIE *bhleu- 'to swell, well up, overflow', itself an extension of *bhel- (2) 'to blow, swell'.
items.cn: fluere 来自原始印欧语 *bhleu-“膨胀、涌起、溢出”的扩展形式，后者又是 *bhel-（第 2 义）“吹、膨胀”的扩展。

items.en: The same root gives fluent, fluid, flux, influence, influx, superfluous and mellifluous; all carry the image of flowing.
items.cn: 同一词根产生 fluent、fluid、flux、influence、influx、superfluous、mellifluous；它们都带着“流动”的意象。

items.en: The verb extends from water to prices, rates, moods, currencies and economies. The noun fluctuation keeps the wave image explicit.
items.cn: 这个动词从水面延伸到价格、比率、情绪、货币和经济。名词 fluctuation 保留了明确的波浪意象。

note.en: Look-alikes share the flowing root; near meanings differ in whether the movement is up and down, back and forth, or simply changing.
note.cn: 形近词共享“流动”词根；近义词的区别在于运动是上下、来回，还是单纯变化。

entries.definition: an instance of rising and falling. It is fluctuate + -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 一次起伏、波动。它是 fluctuate + -ion。

entries.definition: flowing easily, especially of speech. It shares fluere 'to flow' but has nothing to do with rising and falling.
entries.definitionCN: 流畅的，尤指言语。它共享 fluere“流动”，但与上下起伏无关。

entries.definition: a substance that flows; also 'changeable'. The adjective sense overlaps with fluctuating but does not imply repeated rise and fall.
entries.definitionCN: 流体；也指“易变的”。其形容词义与 fluctuating 重叠，但不含反复升降之意。

entries.definition: continuous change; also a flow or discharge. It names the flow itself rather than the up-and-down movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不断变化；也指流动或通量。它指流动本身，而不是上下运动。

entries.definition: to change or differ. It is broader and does not require a repeated up-and-down pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 变化；不同。它更宽泛，不要求反复上下波动。

entries.definition: to swing regularly between two points. It is more mechanical and regular than fluctuate.
entries.definitionCN: 在两点之间规律摆动。它比 fluctuate 更机械、更规则。

entries.definition: to be uncertain or unsteady, especially in opinion. It stresses hesitation, while fluctuate stresses changing level.
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决；动摇，尤指意见。它强调迟疑，而 fluctuate 强调水平变化。

entries.definition: to move back and forth in a wide arc. It is more physical and usually larger than a fluctuation.
entries.definitionCN: 大幅度来回摆动。它更物理，幅度通常比 fluctuation 大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real fluere / fluctus wave image and the real related words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 fluere / fluctus 波浪意象和相关词。

normal.en: fluctus means 'wave': anything that rises and falls like water fluctuates.
normal.cn: fluctus 意为“波浪”：任何像水一样起落的东西都在 fluctuate。

normal.en: Fluent, fluid, flux and fluctuate all come from fluere 'to flow'; the wave is the shape the flow makes.
normal.cn: fluent、fluid、flux、fluctuate 都来自 fluere“流动”；波浪是流动形成的形状。

normal.en: Fluctuation is the noun: a price chart with peaks and troughs shows fluctuation.
normal.cn: fluctuation 是名词：有峰有谷的价格图显示的就是波动。

normal.en: Fluctuate between hope and fear is to move from one crest to the other without settling.
normal.cn: 在希望与恐惧之间 fluctuate，就是从一个波峰移到另一个波峰，始终不停定。

normal.en: A fluctuating demand curve is one that will not stay flat.
normal.cn: fluctuating demand 就是无法保持平直的需求曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a cork on water: it rises, falls, rises again, never resting at one height. That cork is fluctuating.
abstract.cn: 想象水面上的软木塞：升起、落下、再升起，从不停在一个高度。这个软木塞就在 fluctuate。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line that looks like a wave: every peak and trough is one fluctuation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条像波浪的图表线：每个峰和谷都是一次 fluctuation。

abstract.en: Picture a mood that lifts and drops with the day: feelings fluctuate like weather.
abstract.cn: 想象随一天起落的情绪：心情像天气一样 fluctuate。

examples.en: Demand for the product fluctuates with the seasons.
examples.cn: 该产品的需求随季节波动。

examples.en: Her weight fluctuated by only two kilos.
examples.cn: 她的体重只在两公斤内波动。

examples.en: The exchange rate has fluctuated sharply since the announcement.
examples.cn: 自公告以来汇率剧烈波动。

dict_mnemonic.text: “弗拉克图埃特”——弗拉克图像波浪一样上上下下 → fluctuate 波动、起伏

root: 拉丁 fluere“流动”→ fluctus“波浪”→ fluctuare“像波浪般起伏”，核心是“上下波动”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fluctuate all keep the shape of a wave: something rises, falls, and rises again without settling. Prices, water, numbers, moods and markets can all draw that line.
sensesIntro.cn: fluctuate 的八个义项都保留波浪的形状：某物升起、落下、再升起，始终不定。价格、水位、数字、情绪和市场都能画出这条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave line that goes up and down and never stays flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上下起伏、始终不平的波浪线。

branches.en: MARKETS AND NUMBERS: prices, rates, sales and currencies are plotted as lines that swing.
branches.cn: 市场与数字：价格、比率、销量和货币被画成摆动的线。

branches.en: MEASURED LEVELS: water, temperature, quality and attendance all move within a range.
branches.cn: 可测水平：水位、温度、质量和出勤率都在一定范围内变动。

branches.en: INNER LIFE: opinions and moods rise and fall without any number attached.
branches.cn: 内心：意见与情绪的起落，并不附着于任何数字。

branches.en: LITERAL WAVE: the original physical movement of a water surface.
branches.cn: 字面波浪：水面原本的物理运动。

branches.en: BETWEEN TWO POLES: the crest and trough of one wave become hope and fear, or one policy and another.
branches.cn: 两极之间：一个波浪的峰与谷变成希望与恐惧，或两种政策。

intro.en: Fluctuate is a Latin verb in -ate built on fluctus. English adds -ion, -ing, -ant, -al and -ly, but the root does the work.
intro.cn: fluctuate 是建立在 fluctus 上的拉丁 -ate 动词。英语加 -ion、-ing、-ant、-al、-ly，但主要靠词根表义。

latinIntro.en: The fluere family is large: fluctus 'wave', fluere 'flow', fluvius 'river', fluentum 'stream'. English has fluent, fluid, flux, influence and superfluous from the same source.
latinIntro.cn: fluere 词族庞大：fluctus“波浪”、fluere“流动”、fluvius“河流”、fluentum“水流”。英语的 fluent、fluid、flux、influence、superfluous 同出一源。

items.meaning: to move in waves; to rise and fall
items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（fluctus“波浪”+ -ate 动词后缀）
items.example: Prices fluctuate every day.
items.exampleCN: 价格每天波动。

items.meaning: a rise and fall; an irregular change
items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Small fluctuations in temperature are normal.
items.exampleCN: 温度的小幅波动是正常的。

items.meaning: changing up and down continuously
items.meaningCN: 波动的；起伏不定的（-ing 构成形容词）
items.example: A fluctuating supply makes planning hard.
items.exampleCN: 供给波动让规划变得困难。

items.meaning: moving in waves; unstable
items.meaningCN: 波动的；起伏的（-ant 构成形容词，医学中也指可移动的）
items.example: The fluctuant mass shifted under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 那个可移动的肿块在按压下移位。

items.meaning: caused by or relating to fluctuation
items.meaningCN: 波动引起的；涨落性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Fluctuational noise is hard to filter.
items.exampleCN: 涨落噪声很难滤除。

items.meaning: in a fluctuating manner
items.meaningCN: 波动地；起伏不定地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The signal fluctuatedly dropped and rose.
items.exampleCN: 信号起伏不定地下降又上升。

items.meaning: flowing smoothly, especially of speech
items.meaningCN: 流畅的，尤指言语（fluere + -ent）
items.example: She is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 她能流利地说三种语言。

items.meaning: a substance that flows; able to change
items.meaningCN: 流体；易变的（fluere + -id）
items.example: The patient needs fluids.
items.exampleCN: 病人需要补充液体。

items.meaning: continuous change; a flow
items.meaningCN: 不断变化；流动；通量（拉丁 fluxus“流动”）
items.example: The system is in a state of flux.
items.exampleCN: 这个系统处于不断变化之中。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 流动；流泻；奔流（fluctuate 的最终词根）
波浪；巨浪；涌动（英语 fluctuate 的直接来源）
起伏；像波浪般运动（英语 fluctuate 的直接拉丁动词）
河流；溪流（同根词，英语 fluvial 的来源）

definition_zh: 焦点；重点；中心；集中（注意力）；调焦
definition_en: the centre of attention or convergence, or to direct attention or a lens toward one point
core_image: 所有光线汇聚到同一点
scene: 投影屏幕上高亮着三个数字，附录文件放在一旁。 In the report she put the focus on the three most important figures and left the rest to an appendix.
sceneCN: 这里 focus 是「重点、注意力的中心」（第 1 个义项：注意力集中的对象）；句意：在汇报中，她把重点放在三个最重要的数据上，其余细节放进附录。

derivatives.zh: 重新聚焦；重新调整重点

senses.title: Centre of attention
senses.definition: the person or thing that people are most interested in or paying attention to
senses.definitionCN: 人们最感兴趣或最关注的人或事物
senses.example: The focus of the meeting was the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 会议的重点是预算。
senses.why: Latin focus meant 'hearth, fireplace', the burning point of a house. Kepler (1604) used it for the point where rays converge, and by 1796 it meant the centre of activity or energy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 focus 意为“壁炉、火塘”，即房屋中燃烧的那一点。开普勒（1604）用它指光线汇聚之点，到 1796 年它已指活动或能量的中心。

senses.title: Optics: the point of convergence
senses.definition: the point at which light rays meet after passing through a lens or reflecting from a mirror
senses.definitionCN: 光线经透镜或镜面反射后相交的那一点
senses.example: The lens brings the rays to a focus.
senses.exampleCN: 透镜把光线汇聚到焦点。
senses.why: Kepler took the word in 1604, probably by analogy with the burning point of a lens, where sunlight concentrates enough to start a fire.
senses.whyCN: 开普勒在 1604 年引入此义，可能是类比透镜的“燃烧点”——阳光在那里集中到足以起火。

senses.title: A clear image: in focus
senses.definition: the state of an image being sharp because the lens is correctly adjusted
senses.definitionCN: 因镜头调整正确而使影像清晰的状态
senses.example: The photograph is sharp and in focus.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片清晰且对焦准确。
senses.why: When rays meet exactly at the focus, the image is sharp. 'In focus' names that successful convergence.
senses.whyCN: 当光线正好汇聚在焦点上，影像就清晰。in focus 指的就是这次成功的汇聚。

senses.title: Verb: concentrate attention
senses.definition: to direct your attention or effort toward one thing
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力或努力集中到一件事上
senses.example: Focus on the main idea, not the details.
senses.exampleCN: 把注意力放在主旨上，而不是细节。
senses.why: The optical convergence becomes mental: many possible thoughts are brought to one point, as rays are brought to one point.
senses.whyCN: 光学的汇聚变成心智的汇聚：许多可能的念头被收到一点，正如光线被收到一点。

senses.title: Verb: adjust a lens
senses.definition: to adjust a lens or instrument so that the image becomes clear
senses.definitionCN: 调整镜头或仪器，使影像变得清晰
senses.example: He focused the camera on the bird.
senses.exampleCN: 他把相机对准那只鸟并对焦。
senses.why: The verb appears in 1775 in optics: the user moves the lens until the rays meet at the focus.
senses.whyCN: 动词在 1775 年出现于光学：使用者移动镜头，直到光线汇聚在焦点。

senses.title: Geology: the focus of an earthquake
senses.definition: the point inside the earth where an earthquake begins
senses.definitionCN: 地震在地下开始的那一点
senses.example: The quake's focus was ten kilometres deep.
senses.exampleCN: 这次地震的震源深十公里。
senses.why: Energy radiates from one underground point, as light radiates from a focus. The word for the meeting point becomes the word for the starting point.
senses.whyCN: 能量从地下的一点向外辐射，正如光从焦点辐射。表示“汇聚点”的词变成了表示“起点”的词。

senses.title: A centre of activity
senses.definition: the main place or hub where an activity happens
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动发生的主要地点或枢纽
senses.example: The city became the focus of trade in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市成为该地区的贸易中心。
senses.why: The sense 'centre of activity or energy' is recorded from 1796, an extension of the optical image to social and economic life.
senses.whyCN: “活动或能量的中心”这一义项记录于 1796 年，是光学意象向社会与经济生活的延伸。

senses.title: Geometry: a focus of a curve
senses.definition: one of the fixed points used to define an ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola
senses.definitionCN: 用来定义椭圆、抛物线或双曲线的一个定点
senses.example: An ellipse has two foci.
senses.exampleCN: 椭圆有两个焦点。
senses.why: Kepler's mathematical sense survives in geometry: the curve is defined by its relation to these fixed points.
senses.whyCN: 开普勒的数学义项在几何中保留下来：曲线由它与这些定点的关系来定义。

senses.title: Medicine: a focus of infection
senses.definition: a localized point in the body where an infection or disease is concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 体内感染或疾病集中的局部位置
senses.example: Doctors found a focus of infection in the lung.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在肺部发现了一个感染灶。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the optical image: disease activity is concentrated at one point, from which it may spread.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用光学意象：疾病活动集中在一点，并可能从那里扩散。

intro.en: Focus is Latin for 'hearth, fireplace'. Its optical and mental senses are early modern additions; the deeper origin of the Latin word is unknown.
intro.cn: focus 在拉丁语中意为“壁炉、火塘”。它的光学与心智义项是近代早期的添加；这个拉丁词更早的来源不明。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'point of convergence', from Latin focus 'hearth, fireplace' (also figuratively 'home, family'). Introduced by Hobbes in the 1650s.
items.cn: 最早记录为“汇聚点”，来自拉丁语 focus“壁炉、火塘”（引申为“家、家庭”）。17 世纪 50 年代由霍布斯引入英语。

items.en: Latin focus 'hearth, fireplace' is of unknown origin. In post-classical times it was also used for 'fire' itself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 focus“壁炉、火塘”来源不明。在后古典时期，它也被用来指“火”本身。

items.en: Kepler takes the word in a mathematical sense for 'point of convergence', perhaps by analogy with the burning point of a lens. The purely optical sense may have existed earlier but is not recorded.
items.cn: 开普勒在 1604 年把它用作数学意义的“汇聚点”，可能是类比透镜的燃烧点。纯光学的义项可能存在得更早，但没有记录。

items.en: The verb appears in optics in 1775 ('bring into focus'), and in the figurative sense in 1807. The intransitive use follows by 1864.
items.cn: 动词在 1775 年出现于光学（“使对焦”），1807 年出现比喻义。不及物用法到 1864 年出现。

items.en: The sense 'centre of activity or energy' is recorded from 1796, and the medical 'focus of infection' follows. The plural is focuses or the Latin foci.
items.cn: “活动或能量的中心”义记录于 1796 年，医学的“感染灶”随后出现。复数形式为 focuses 或拉丁式 foci。

note.en: Look-alikes share the optical or Latin vocabulary; near meanings differ in whether they name attention, a centre, or a point of origin.
note.cn: 形近词共享光学或拉丁词汇；近义词的区别在于指注意力、中心还是起点。

entries.definition: relating to a focus. It is focus + -al, and is common in 'focal point'.
entries.definitionCN: 与焦点有关的。它是 focus + -al，常见于 focal point。

entries.definition: the Latin plural of focus, used especially in geometry and medicine. Focuses is the ordinary English plural.
entries.definitionCN: focus 的拉丁式复数，尤用于几何和医学。focuses 是普通英语复数。

entries.definition: the regular English plural and third-person singular. It is the safer form outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 规则英语复数和第三人称单数。在非技术写作中更稳妥。

entries.definition: giving clear attention, or adjusted so that an image is sharp. It is focus + -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 专注的，或已对焦清晰的。它是 focus + -ed。

entries.definition: to bring your attention or effort together on one thing. It is close to focus as a verb but can also mean to make a liquid stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 把注意力或努力集中到一件事上。作动词时与 focus 接近，但也可指使液体浓缩。

entries.definition: the middle point or main place of something. It is more spatial than focus, which can be purely attentional.
entries.definitionCN: 中间点或主要地点。它比 focus 更偏空间，而 focus 可以纯指注意力。

entries.definition: special importance given to something. It stresses weight or priority, not the point where attention converges.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某事物的特别重要性。它强调分量或优先，而不是注意力汇聚的那一点。

entries.definition: the point on the surface directly above an earthquake's focus. It is above the focus, not the same point.
entries.definitionCN: 震源正上方的地表点。它在震源之上，而不是同一个点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin 'hearth' origin, Kepler's optical sense, and the real modern derivatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁“火塘”来源、开普勒的光学义，以及真实的现代派生词。

normal.en: Latin focus was the hearth, the burning point of a house; Kepler made it the point where light burns.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 focus 是火塘，房屋中燃烧的那一点；开普勒把它变成光线“燃烧”的那一点。

normal.en: In focus means the rays meet exactly on the film, so the image is sharp.
normal.cn: in focus 指光线正好汇聚在胶片上，所以影像清晰。

normal.en: Focus on the main idea is the mental version: bring many thoughts to one point.
normal.cn: focus on the main idea 是心智版本：把许多念头收到一点。

normal.en: The focus of an earthquake is where the energy starts; the epicentre is directly above it.
normal.cn: 地震的 focus 是能量开始之处；epicentre 在它正上方。

normal.en: Focal point and focal length come from the same optical image of converging rays.
normal.cn: focal point 与 focal length 都来自同一个光线汇聚的光学意象。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass burning a dot on paper: all the sunlight is gathered into one bright point, and that point is the focus.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜在纸上烧出一个点：所有阳光被聚成一个亮点，这个点就是 focus。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd all turning to one speaker: attention converges like light, and the speaker becomes the focus.
abstract.cn: 想象人群都转向同一位演讲者：注意力像光一样汇聚，演讲者成为 focus。

abstract.en: Picture a single lamp in a dark room: everything else recedes and the lamp is the centre of activity.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里唯一的一盏灯：其余都退去，这盏灯就是活动的中心。

examples.en: The discussion shifted focus from cost to safety.
examples.cn: 讨论的重点从成本转向了安全。

examples.en: Try to focus on one task at a time.
examples.cn: 试着一次只专注于一项任务。

examples.en: The picture is out of focus because the lens moved.
examples.cn: 因为镜头移动了，照片失焦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “福克斯”——福克斯把灯光都聚到舞台中央那一点 → focus 焦点、集中

root: 拉丁 focus“壁炉、火塘”，即屋中燃烧的那一点；经开普勒引申为光线汇聚的“焦点”，再引申为注意力中心。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of focus all come from one optical image: many rays, or many thoughts, are brought to a single point.
sensesIntro.cn: focus 的九个义项都来自同一个光学意象：许多光线，或许多念头，被收到同一点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered rays converge on one point, and everything else falls away.
core.cn: 核心意象：散乱的光线汇聚到一点，其余一切都退去。

branches.en: OPTICS: rays meet at a point, a lens is adjusted until they do, and the image becomes sharp.
branches.cn: 光学：光线在一点相交，调整镜头直到它们相交，影像就清晰。

branches.en: ATTENTION: many possible objects of thought are reduced to one, which becomes the focus.
branches.cn: 注意力：许多可能的思考对象被减到一个，它成为 focus。

branches.en: A POINT OF ORIGIN: an earthquake or an infection starts at one localized point and spreads.
branches.cn: 起点：地震或感染从一个局部点开始并扩散。

branches.en: A CENTRE: the place where activity or energy gathers, as a city becomes a trade focus.
branches.cn: 中心：活动或能量聚集之地，如城市成为贸易中心。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: a curve is defined by fixed points called foci.
branches.cn: 几何：曲线由称为焦点的定点来定义。

intro.en: Focus is a Latin noun used directly as a verb. English adds -ed, -ing, -al, and the prefixes re- and un-.
intro.cn: focus 是直接作动词用的拉丁名词。英语加 -ed、-ing、-al，以及前缀 re-、un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin focus 'hearth' has no large derived family of its own; the modern words are English formations. The optical vocabulary (focal, foci) is the main Latin-style extension.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 focus“火塘”本身没有庞大的派生词族；现代词都是英语构造。光学词汇（focal、foci）是主要的拉丁式延伸。

items.meaning: a point of convergence; to converge attention
items.meaningCN: 焦点；集中（直接来自拉丁 focus“火塘”）
items.example: Keep your focus on the goal.
items.exampleCN: 把注意力集中在目标上。

items.meaning: concentrated; adjusted to be sharp
items.meaningCN: 专注的；已对焦的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: She gave a focused answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给出了一个重点明确的回答。

items.meaning: the act of concentrating or adjusting
items.meaningCN: 聚焦；调焦；集中注意力（-ing 形式）
items.example: Focusing takes practice.
items.exampleCN: 专注需要练习。

items.meaning: relating to a focus
items.meaningCN: 焦点的；关键的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: She is the focal point of the team.
items.exampleCN: 她是团队的核心人物。

items.meaning: to bring into focus; to concentrate
items.meaningCN: 使聚焦；使集中（-ize 表示“使成为”）
items.example: The lens focalizes the beam.
items.exampleCN: 透镜使光束聚焦。

items.meaning: to focus again or change the point of attention
items.meaningCN: 重新对焦；重新调整重点（re-“再次”）
items.example: The company refocused on its core business.
items.exampleCN: 公司重新聚焦于核心业务。

items.meaning: not sharp; lacking a clear aim
items.meaningCN: 未对焦的；缺乏重点的（un-“不”+ focused）
items.example: The plan was vague and unfocused.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划含糊而缺乏重点。

items.meaning: a camera system that focuses itself
items.meaningCN: 自动对焦（auto-“自动”+ focus）
items.example: The phone's autofocus is fast.
items.exampleCN: 这款手机的自动对焦很快。

items.meaning: without a focus or clear centre
items.meaningCN: 没有焦点的；缺乏中心的（-less 表示“没有”）
items.example: The essay felt focusless.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章让人感觉没有重点。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 壁炉；火塘；引申为家（英语 focus 的直接来源）
火塘的；焦点的（拉丁式形容词，英语 focal 的模型）

latinEntries.meaning: hearths; in modern science, focal points
latinEntries.meaningCN: 多个火塘；现代科学中的焦点（拉丁复数）

definition_zh: 公式；方程式；配方；方案；套话
definition_en: a set expression or rule, especially a mathematical equation, a chemical expression, or a fixed way of doing something
core_image: 一张写满符号的纸：把复杂过程压缩成可重复的形式
scene: 黑板上写着水的组成，讲台上摆着分子模型。 On the blackboard the teacher wrote the chemical formula of water, H2O, and asked the students to build two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom with models.
sceneCN: 这里 formula 是「化学式」（第 2 个义项：用符号表示物质组成的式子）；句意：老师在黑板上写下水的化学式 H₂O，让学生用模型拼出两个氢原子和一个氧原子。

pos.zh: 固定说法；套话；惯用模式

senses.title: A mathematical expression
senses.definition: a set of symbols and numbers expressing a rule or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 用符号和数字表达规则或关系的式子
senses.example: The formula gives the area of a circle.
senses.exampleCN: 这个公式给出圆的面积。
senses.why: The mathematical sense is recorded from 1796. A formula is a small fixed 'form' into which different numbers can be put, and the result follows every time.
senses.whyCN: 数学义记录于 1796 年。formula 是一个小小的固定“形式”，把不同数字代进去，结果每次都按同样规则得出。

senses.title: A chemical formula
senses.definition: a written set of chemical symbols showing the composition of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 用化学符号写出的、表示物质组成的式子
senses.example: The formula for water is H2O.
senses.exampleCN: 水的化学式是 H₂O。
senses.why: Chemistry adopted the word in 1842: the symbols are a compact form that stands for the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 化学在 1842 年采用这个词：符号是一种紧凑的形式，代表物质本身。

senses.title: A recipe or method
senses.definition: a list of ingredients and steps for making something
senses.definitionCN: 制作某物所需的配料与步骤清单
senses.example: The formula for the sauce is a family secret.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酱料的配方是家族秘密。
senses.why: From 1706 formula meant 'a prescription, a recipe'. A recipe is a fixed form that, followed exactly, produces the same result.
senses.whyCN: 从 1706 年起，formula 意为“处方、配方”。配方就是一个固定形式，照做就能得到同样的结果。

senses.title: Baby formula
senses.definition: a manufactured milk preparation designed to feed babies
senses.definitionCN: 为喂养婴儿而配制的代乳品
senses.example: The baby was fed formula from a bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 这个婴儿用奶瓶喝配方奶。
senses.why: Infant formula is literally a formulated product: its ingredients are set by a controlled recipe to imitate human milk.
senses.whyCN: infant formula 字面就是“按配方配制的产品”：其成分按受控配方设定，以模拟母乳。

senses.title: A fixed set of words
senses.definition: a set form of words used in a ceremony, ritual, or legal document
senses.definitionCN: 用于仪式、典礼或法律文件的固定说法
senses.example: The priest recited the ancient formula.
senses.exampleCN: 神父诵读了古老的仪式用语。
senses.why: This is the word's first English sense in the 1630s: 'words used in a ceremony or ritual', from Latin formula 'a rule, method, small form'.
senses.whyCN: 这是 17 世纪 30 年代英语中最早的义项：“仪式中使用的词句”，来自拉丁语 formula“规则、方法、小形式”。

senses.title: A plan for success
senses.titleCN: 成功之道；行之有效的方案
senses.definition: a proven set of steps or principles that is expected to produce a good result
senses.definitionCN: 一套经证实、预期能带来好结果的步骤或原则
senses.example: There is no simple formula for a happy marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福的婚姻没有简单的公式。
senses.why: Once a method reliably produces a result, it is treated like a mathematical formula: put in the same elements, get the same outcome.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种方法能稳定产生结果，它就被当作数学公式：投入同样的要素，得到同样的结果。

senses.title: Motor racing: a class of car
senses.definition: a class or specification of racing car, usually defined by engine size
senses.definitionCN: 按发动机排量等标准划分的赛车等级或规格
senses.example: He raced in Formula Two for three seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 他在二级方程式赛车中跑了三个赛季。
senses.why: The racing sense is from 1927: each class is defined by a fixed specification, a formula that every car in the class must follow.
senses.whyCN: 赛车义始于 1927 年：每个等级由固定规格定义，这就是该等级每辆车都必须遵守的 formula。

senses.title: A formulaic phrase
senses.definition: a phrase used automatically, without fresh thought, often in the adjective formulaic
senses.definitionCN: 不加新思考、自动套用的说法，常以形容词 formulaic 出现
senses.example: His apology sounded like a formula.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听起来像套话。
senses.why: Carlyle's 1837 use gave the word a critical edge: a rule followed slavishly without understanding. The fixed form has become empty.
senses.whyCN: 卡莱尔 1837 年的用法赋予这个词批评意味：不加理解地死守规则。固定的形式由此变得空洞。

intro.en: Formula is Latin for 'small form', a diminutive of forma. The word moved from ritual words to recipes, mathematics, chemistry, and racing. The origin of forma itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: formula 是拉丁语“小形式”，是 forma 的指小词。这个词从仪式用语走到配方、数学、化学和赛车。forma 本身的来源不确定。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'words used in a ceremony or ritual', earlier appearing as a Latin word in English texts.
items.cn: 最早记录为“仪式或典礼中使用的词句”，更早则以拉丁词形式出现在英语文本中。

items.en: Latin formula 'form, draft, contract, regulation', in law 'a rule, method', literally 'small form', a diminutive of forma 'form'. Forma is of unknown origin; one theory links it to Greek morphe 'form' via Etruscan, but this is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 formula“形式、草稿、契约、规定”，法律中为“规则、方法”，字面是“小形式”，是 forma“形式”的指小词。forma 来源不明；一种理论认为它经伊特鲁里亚语与希腊语 morphe“形式”有关，但这属于来源不确定。

items.en: The sense 'a prescription, a recipe' is recorded. The same noun now covers both written rules and lists of ingredients.
items.cn: “处方、配方”义有记录。同一个名词此时既覆盖书面规则，也覆盖配料清单。

items.en: Mathematical use is from 1796; chemical use from 1842. Both are fixed symbolic forms into which values or elements are placed.
items.cn: 数学用法始于 1796 年，化学用法始于 1842 年。两者都是固定的符号形式，用来代入数值或元素。

items.en: Carlyle's 1837 use adds the critical sense 'rule followed without understanding'. Motor racing adopts formula for a car class in 1927.
items.cn: 卡莱尔 1837 年的用法增加了批评义“不加理解地遵守的规则”。赛车界在 1927 年用 formula 指车辆等级。

note.en: Look-alikes share forma or sound; near meanings differ in whether they name a rule, a recipe, or a mere pattern.
note.cn: 形近词共享 forma 或读音；近义词的区别在于指规则、配方还是单纯模式。

entries.definition: shape, document, or a way of doing something. Formula is the diminutive 'small form', so form is the broader parent word.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、表格，或做事方式。formula 是“小形式”，因此 form 是更宽泛的母词。

entries.definition: to express an idea precisely, or to create a formula. It is formula + -ate.
entries.definitionCN: 精确表述想法，或制定配方。它是 formula + -ate。

entries.definition: made according to a fixed pattern; unoriginal. It is formula + -ic.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定模式制作的；缺乏新意的。它是 formula + -ic。

entries.definition: the Latin plural of formula, common in academic writing. Formulas is the ordinary English plural.
entries.definitionCN: formula 的拉丁式复数，常用于学术写作。formulas 是普通英语复数。

entries.definition: a statement that two expressions are equal. It is a kind of formula, but a formula need not contain an equality sign.
entries.definitionCN: 表示两个表达式相等的陈述。它是公式的一种，但公式不一定含等号。

entries.definition: a set of instructions for cooking a dish. It matches formula in the ingredient sense but is rarely used for mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 烹饪一道菜的步骤说明。它在配料义上与 formula 对应，但很少用于数学。

entries.definition: a systematic way of doing something. It is broader and less rigid than a formula.
entries.definitionCN: 系统的做事方式。它比 formula 更宽泛，也不那么僵硬。

entries.definition: a repeated arrangement or model. It stresses repetition, while formula stresses a rule that produces a result.
entries.definitionCN: 重复的排列或模式。它强调重复，而 formula 强调产生结果的规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin forma / formula pair and the real modern applications.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁 forma / formula 对应，以及真实的现代应用。

normal.en: Formula is a 'small form': a compact written pattern that stands for a larger process.
normal.cn: formula 是“小形式”：一个紧凑的书面模式，代表一个更大的过程。

normal.en: The same word covers a ritual sentence, a cake recipe, a maths equation, and a racing class: all are fixed forms.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖仪式语句、蛋糕配方、数学方程和赛车等级：它们都是固定形式。

normal.en: In chemistry, H2O is a formula because the symbols stand for the substance in compressed form.
normal.cn: 化学中 H₂O 是 formula，因为符号以压缩形式代表该物质。

normal.en: A formula for success treats life like a recipe: follow the set steps and expect the result.
normal.cn: a formula for success 把生活当作配方：照设定步骤做，期待相应结果。

normal.en: Formulaic speech is a formula that has lost its thought; the form remains but the meaning is automatic.
normal.cn: formulaic 言语是失去思考的 formula：形式还在，意义却已自动化。

abstract.en: Picture a stencil: it is a small fixed form, and whatever you paint through it comes out in the same shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一块镂空模板：它是一个固定的小形式，无论用什么颜料，透出来的形状都一样。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe card and an equation on the same wall: both are instructions compressed into a repeatable pattern.
abstract.cn: 想象同一面墙上挂着配方卡和方程式：两者都是压缩成可重复模式的说明。

abstract.en: Picture a race car built exactly to a specification sheet: the sheet is the formula that defines the class.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆完全按规格表制造的赛车：规格表就是定义该等级的 formula。

examples.en: The formula for the area of a triangle is half the base times the height.
examples.cn: 三角形面积的公式是底乘以高的一半。

examples.en: No single formula guarantees a good outcome.
examples.cn: 没有单一的公式能保证好结果。

examples.en: The company reformulated the product to cut sugar.
examples.cn: 公司重新调整配方以减少糖分。

dict_mnemonic.text: “佛缪拉”——佛缪拉把复杂算式压成一行小字 → formula 公式

root: 拉丁 forma“形式”的指小词 formula“小形式”，核心是“把复杂内容压缩成固定可重复的形式”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of formula all name a fixed form: words, ingredients, symbols, specifications, or a method that can be repeated.
sensesIntro.cn: formula 的八个义项都指一种固定形式：词句、配料、符号、规格，或可重复的方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compact fixed pattern into which different contents can be placed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个紧凑的固定模式，可以往里放入不同内容。

branches.en: SYMBOLS: maths and chemistry compress a relationship or a substance into a short written form.
branches.cn: 符号：数学和化学把一种关系或物质压缩成简短的书面形式。

branches.en: INGREDIENTS: a recipe and infant formula are lists of contents fixed by proportion.
branches.cn: 配料：配方和婴儿配方奶都是按比例固定的成分清单。

branches.en: WORDS: ritual sentences and clichés are forms of speech repeated without fresh thought.
branches.cn: 词句：仪式语句和套话是不加新思考而重复的言语形式。

branches.en: METHOD: a proven procedure is treated as a formula for producing a result.
branches.cn: 方法：经证实的程序被当作产生结果的公式。

branches.en: SPECIFICATION: a racing class is defined by a fixed technical form.
branches.cn: 规格：赛车等级由固定的技术形式来定义。

intro.en: Formula is a Latin diminutive of forma. English builds verbs and nouns with -ate, -ation, adjectives with -ic, and agents with -or.
intro.cn: formula 是 forma 的拉丁指小词。英语用 -ate、-ation 构成动词和名词，用 -ic 构成形容词，用 -or 构成施动者。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma 'form, shape, mould' is the base; formula is its diminutive. The same forma gives form, formal, format and conform; the deeper origin of forma is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma“形式、形状、模子”是词基，formula 是它的指小词。同一个 forma 产生 form、formal、format、conform；forma 的更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: a small form; a fixed rule or expression
items.meaningCN: 小形式；固定规则或表达式（forma + 指小后缀 -ula）
items.example: Learn the formula by heart.
items.exampleCN: 把这个公式背下来。

items.meaning: to express precisely or to create a formula
items.meaningCN: 制定；构想；用公式表达（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: They formulated a clear plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们制定了一个清晰的计划。

items.meaning: the act of expressing or the resulting form
items.meaningCN: 表述；配方；制定（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The formulation of the policy took months.
items.exampleCN: 政策的制定花了几个月。

items.meaning: following a fixed pattern; unoriginal
items.meaningCN: 公式化的；程式化的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The plot is formulaic.
items.exampleCN: 情节很程式化。

items.meaning: in a fixed, unoriginal way
items.meaningCN: 程式化地（-ally 构成副词）
items.example: The speech ended formulaically.
items.exampleCN: 演讲以程式化的方式结束。

items.meaning: a person who formulates something
items.meaningCN: 制定者；配方设计者（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The formulator of the theory was unknown.
items.exampleCN: 该理论的提出者不为人知。

items.meaning: a book of prescribed formulas or medicines
items.meaningCN: 处方集；药典（-ary 表示集合、场所）
items.example: The hospital updated its formulary.
items.exampleCN: 医院更新了处方集。

items.meaning: to formulate again or differently
items.meaningCN: 重新表述；重新制定（re-“再次”）
items.example: They reformulated the question.
items.exampleCN: 他们重新表述了这个问题。

items.meaning: the smallest unit represented by an ionic formula
items.meaningCN: 化学式单位；式量单位（复合名词）
items.example: One formula unit of sodium chloride contains two ions.
items.exampleCN: 一个氯化钠化学式单位包含两个离子。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 形式；形状；模式；模子（formula 的母词）

latinEntries.meaning: a small form; a rule, draft, contract
latinEntries.meaningCN: 小形式；规则；草稿；契约（英语 formula 的直接来源）
公式的；规则的（拉丁式形容词）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：程式化的文书。

definition_zh: 地基；基础；基金会；建立；粉底
definition_en: the solid base under a building, the basic principle something rests on, or an institution set up with an endowment
core_image: 埋在土里的石基：上面的一切都压在它身上
scene: 工地上，钢筋笼和水平尺摆在挖好的基坑旁。 The workers first poured the concrete foundation and then built the walls on it, so the house would not sink.
sceneCN: 这里 foundation 是「建筑物的地基」（第 1 个义项：支撑建筑的坚固底座）；句意：工人先浇筑混凝土地基，再在上面砌墙，这样房子才不会下沉。

senses.title: The solid base of a building
senses.definition: the strong lower part of a building that carries its weight and fixes it in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 承载建筑重量并把它固定在地下的坚固下部结构
senses.example: The foundation was poured before the walls went up.
senses.exampleCN: 墙体砌起之前先浇筑了地基。
senses.why: Latin fundus means 'bottom, foundation'. The first physical sense is the bottom on which everything above rests.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fundus 意为“底部、基础”。第一个物理义项就是承载上方一切的底部。

senses.title: The basis of an idea or system
senses.definition: the central principle or set of facts that supports a belief, subject, or system
senses.definitionCN: 支撑信念、学科或制度的核心原则或事实基础
senses.example: Trust is the foundation of a good team.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是优秀团队的基础。
senses.why: Remove the physical base and the building falls; remove the supporting principle and the idea falls. The metaphor is direct.
senses.whyCN: 抽掉物理底座，建筑会倒；抽掉支撑性原则，观念会倒。这个比喻非常直接。

senses.title: An endowed institution
senses.definition: an organization established with money set aside to support its work
senses.definitionCN: 以专门留出的资金支持其工作的组织
senses.example: The foundation funds medical research.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金会资助医学研究。
senses.why: From the late 14c. the word meant 'establishment of an institution with an endowment'; the money is the base that keeps the institution standing.
senses.whyCN: 从 14 世纪晚期起，这个词指“以捐赠基金设立机构”；这笔钱就是让机构站稳的“地基”。

senses.title: The act of founding
senses.definition: the act of establishing an institution, city, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 设立机构、城市或组织的行为
senses.example: The foundation of the university dates from 1636.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的创建可追溯到 1636 年。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, 'action of founding', from Latin fundatio. To found is to lay the bottom of something new.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项“创立行为”，来自拉丁语 fundatio。创立就是为新生事物铺设底部。

senses.title: Makeup base
senses.definition: a coloured cream applied to the face as a base for other makeup
senses.definitionCN: 涂在脸上、作为其他妆容底层的有色乳霜
senses.example: She applied foundation before the powder.
senses.exampleCN: 她先上粉底，再扑粉。
senses.why: The cosmetics sense is from 1910, probably short for foundation makeup: the cream is literally the base layer under the rest.
senses.whyCN: 化妆品义始于 1910 年，可能是 foundation makeup 的缩写：这种乳霜字面上就是其余妆容下面的底层。

senses.title: The basics of a subject
senses.definition: in the plural, the basic facts or skills that a subject rests on
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指某学科所依赖的基本事实或技能
senses.example: The course covers the foundations of chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授化学的基础。
senses.why: The plural foundations names the set of supporting elements, just as a building has several foundation walls.
senses.whyCN: 复数 foundations 指一组支撑性要素，正如建筑有多道基础墙。

senses.title: Underlying groundwork
senses.definition: the work or structure laid down first, on which later work depends
senses.definitionCN: 先铺设好的工作或结构，后续工作依赖它
senses.example: The research laid the groundwork, the foundation for the new drug.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究为新药打下了基础。
senses.why: Any later structure needs something under it. Foundation can name that earlier supporting work, not only stone and concrete.
senses.whyCN: 任何后来的结构都需要下方有东西。foundation 可以指先前的支撑性工作，而不只是石头和混凝土。

senses.title: A foundation garment
senses.definition: an undergarment such as a corset or girdle that shapes the body
senses.definitionCN: 紧身胸衣、束腹等塑造身体线条的内衣
senses.example: The museum displays foundation garments from the 1900s.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了 20 世纪初的塑形内衣。
senses.why: A garment worn underneath is the base layer of dress, so the old trade term for corsetry borrows the building image.
senses.whyCN: 穿在里面的衣物是服装的底层，因此旧时内衣行业借用了建筑意象。

senses.title: The base layer of a road
senses.definition: the compacted layer under a road or pavement that spreads the load
senses.definitionCN: 道路或铺面下方、分散荷载的压实层
senses.example: The road failed because its foundation was too thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路损坏是因为基层太薄。
senses.why: Engineering keeps the literal sense: whatever is under the surface and carries the load is the foundation.
senses.whyCN: 工程学保留字面义：位于表面之下、承载荷载的层就是 foundation。

intro.en: Foundation comes from Latin fundatio, from fundare 'to lay a bottom', from fundus 'bottom'. The family is regular, and the physical sense is the ancestor of all the others.
intro.cn: foundation 来自拉丁语 fundatio，出自 fundare“铺设底部”，再出自 fundus“底部”。词族规则，物理义项是其余义项的祖先。

items.en: First recorded as 'action of founding', from Old French fondacion or directly from Latin fundationem, noun of action from fundare.
items.cn: 最早记录为“创立行为”，来自古法语 fondacion，或直接来自拉丁语 fundationem，即 fundare 的动作名词。

items.en: Fundare 'to lay a bottom or foundation' comes from fundus 'bottom, foundation, piece of land', from PIE *bhudh- 'bottom, base'.
items.cn: fundare“铺设底部或地基”来自 fundus“底部、基础、一块土地”，再源自原始印欧语 *bhudh-“底部、基底”。

items.en: The specialized sense 'establishment of an institution with an endowment' appears in the late 14c.; 'that which is founded' (a college, hospital) from the 1510s; 'funds endowed for charitable purposes' from the early 15c.
items.cn: “以捐赠基金设立机构”这一专门义见于 14 世纪晚期；“被创立之物”（学院、医院）始于 16 世纪 10 年代；“用于慈善的捐赠基金”始于 15 世纪早期。

items.en: The sense 'solid base of a structure' is recorded. The Latin word was glossed in Old English by staþol, 'foundation, base'.
items.cn: “结构的坚固底座”义有记录。这个拉丁词在古英语中曾用 staþol“基础、底座”来对译。

items.en: The cosmetics sense 'coloured cream applied to the face' appears, probably short for foundation makeup. The family also gives fund, fundamental and profound.
items.cn: 化妆品义“涂在脸上的有色乳霜”出现，可能是 foundation makeup 的缩写。这个词族还产生 fund、fundamental、profound。

note.en: Look-alikes share fundus or sound; near meanings differ in whether they name a physical base, a principle, or an institution.
note.cn: 形近词共享 fundus 或读音；近义词的区别在于指物理底座、原则还是机构。

entries.definition: to establish or begin something. It comes from Latin fundare, the verb behind foundation.
entries.definitionCN: 建立；创办。它来自拉丁语 fundare，即 foundation 背后的动词。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside, or to provide money. It is the financial branch of the same 'bottom' root.
entries.definitionCN: 留出的一笔钱，或提供资金。它是同一个“底部”词根的金融分支。

entries.definition: the base or buttocks; a foundation. It is the literal Latin fundamentum, and is now rare or humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 基础；臀部。它是字面的拉丁 fundamentum，现在罕见或带幽默色彩。

entries.definition: a person who establishes an institution. Note that the verb founder 'to sink or fail' is a different word from French fondrer.
entries.definitionCN: 机构的创立者。注意动词 founder“沉没、失败”是另一个词，来自法语 fondrer。

entries.definition: the bottom part on which something stands. It is more physical and less institutional than foundation.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑某物的底部。它比 foundation 更物理，也较少指机构。

entries.definition: the main principle or reason behind something. It is usually abstract, while foundation can be concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物背后的主要原则或理由。它通常抽象，而 foundation 可以是具体的。

entries.definition: the work done first as a base for later work. It stresses preparatory effort rather than structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为后续工作打底的前期工作。它强调准备性努力，而不是结构。

entries.definition: money given to an institution to support it. An endowed foundation lives on this money.
entries.definitionCN: 捐给机构以支持其运作的钱。有基金的基金会靠这笔钱维持。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real fundus 'bottom' family and the real institutional history.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的 fundus“底部”词族，以及真实的机构史。

normal.en: fundus means 'bottom': the foundation is the bottom of a building, and a principle is the bottom of an idea.
normal.cn: fundus 意为“底部”：地基是建筑的底部，原则是观念的地基。

normal.en: Fund, foundation, fundamental and profound all come from the same 'bottom' root.
normal.cn: fund、foundation、fundamental、profound 都来自同一个“底部”词根。

normal.en: A foundation is also an institution with an endowment: the money is the base that keeps it standing.
normal.cn: foundation 也指有捐赠基金的机构：这笔钱是让它站稳的地基。

normal.en: Foundation cream is the base layer of makeup, which is why the cosmetic keeps the same name.
normal.cn: 粉底是妆容的底层，所以化妆品沿用同一个名称。

normal.en: To lay the foundation is to do the first work on which later work will rest.
normal.cn: lay the foundation 就是先做后续工作将要依托的第一步。

abstract.en: Picture a stone block sunk into the earth: everything above presses down on it, and nothing shows but the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一块埋入土中的石块：上方一切都压在它身上，而它只露出顶面。

abstract.en: Picture a tree's roots: unseen, but every branch depends on them. A foundation works the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象树根：看不见，但每根枝条都依赖它。foundation 的作用正是如此。

abstract.en: Picture a table with one leg removed: the top collapses, no matter how fine it looked. That is a missing foundation.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被抽掉一条腿：桌面再漂亮也会塌。这就是 foundation 缺失。

examples.en: The builders checked the foundation before adding the second floor.
examples.cn: 加建二层之前，施工方检查了地基。

examples.en: Early reading skills are the foundation of later learning.
examples.cn: 早期阅读能力是后续学习的基础。

examples.en: A private foundation paid for the restoration.
examples.cn: 一家私人基金会出资修复。

dict_mnemonic.text: “房得深”——房子要得深，地基才打得牢 → foundation 地基、基础

root: 拉丁 fundus“底部、基底”→ fundare“铺设底部”→ fundatio“创立、奠基”，核心是“承托一切的底座”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of foundation all rest on one image: something solid underneath that carries what is above it. The thing above may be a building, a subject, a belief, or an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: foundation 的九个义项都建立在一个意象上：下方有坚固之物承载上方。上方之物可以是建筑、学科、信念或机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid layer underneath, hidden but carrying all the weight above.
core.cn: 核心意象：下方有一层坚固之物，看不见，却承载上方全部重量。

branches.en: PHYSICAL BASE: a building or road rests its load on a compacted lower layer.
branches.cn: 物理底座：建筑或道路把荷载压在密实的下层。

branches.en: PRINCIPLE AND BASICS: a belief or a subject rests on facts and skills that must come first.
branches.cn: 原则与基础：信念或学科，依托必须先具备的事实与技能。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: an endowment is the base that keeps an organization standing; founding is the act of laying that base.
branches.cn: 机构：捐赠基金是让组织站稳的底座；创立就是铺设这个底座的行为。

branches.en: LAYERS OF DRESS: makeup and undergarments are literally the base layers worn beneath others.
branches.cn: 穿戴层次：粉底和内衣字面上就是穿在其余部分之下的底层。

branches.en: GROUNDWORK: the unseen preparatory work on which a later result depends.
branches.cn: 前期工作：看不见的准备性工作，后续结果依赖它。

intro.en: Foundation is fundatio, a Latin noun of action from fundare. English adds -al, -ally, -less, and builds found and founder.
intro.cn: foundation 是 fundatio，来自 fundare 的拉丁动作名词。英语加 -al、-ally、-less，并构造 found 与 founder。

latinIntro.en: The fundus family is broad: fundus 'bottom', fundare 'lay a bottom', fundatio 'a founding', fundamentum 'foundation'. Note that function comes from fungi 'perform', not from fundus.
latinIntro.cn: fundus 词族很广：fundus“底部”、fundare“铺底”、fundatio“创立”、fundamentum“基础”。注意 function 来自 fungi“执行”，不是来自 fundus。

items.meaning: the act of founding; a base; an endowed institution
items.meaningCN: 创立；地基；基金会（fund-“底部”+ -ation 动作名词）
items.example: The foundation took two weeks to set.
items.exampleCN: 地基花了两周凝固。

items.meaning: forming the base; fundamental
items.meaningCN: 基础的；根本的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Reading is a foundational skill.
items.exampleCN: 阅读是一项基础技能。

items.meaning: at the level of basic principles
items.meaningCN: 在基础层面上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two theories are foundationally different.
items.exampleCN: 这两种理论在基础上就不同。

items.meaning: having no base or support
items.meaningCN: 无基础的；无根据的（-less 表示“没有”）
items.example: A foundationless claim is easy to dismiss.
items.exampleCN: 无根据的主张很容易被驳倒。

items.meaning: to establish or begin an institution
items.meaningCN: 建立；创办；奠基（拉丁 fundare“铺底”）
items.example: The city was founded in 1802.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市建于 1802 年。

items.meaning: a person who establishes something
items.meaningCN: 创始人；奠基者（-er 表示人）
items.example: The founder donated the land.
items.exampleCN: 创始人捐赠了这块土地。

items.meaning: the establishing of an institution
items.meaningCN: 创立；建国的（-ing 形式）
items.example: The founding members wrote the rules.
items.exampleCN: 创始成员制定了规则。

items.meaning: a sum of money set aside; to provide money
items.meaningCN: 基金；资助（拉丁 fundus“底部、土地”）
items.example: The fund supports young artists.
items.exampleCN: 该基金支持年轻艺术家。

items.meaning: a base; the buttocks
items.meaningCN: 基础；臀部（拉丁 fundamentum 直接借入，现较少用）
items.example: The fundament of the argument is weak.
items.exampleCN: 这个论证的基础很薄弱。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 底部；基础；一块土地（foundation 的最终词源）
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语例：田地的基础部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to lay the bottom or foundation of
latinEntries.meaningCN: 铺设底部；奠基（英语 found 的来源）
创立；奠基（英语 foundation 的直接来源）
基础；地基；支撑（英语 fundament、fundamental 的来源）

definition_zh: 框架；结构；体系；基本架构
definition_en: a supporting structure or set of basic rules and ideas that something is built around
core_image: 先立起的骨架，后来的一切都挂在它上面
scene: 研究开始前，白板上画着方格，便签和变量箭头贴在对应位置。 Before the study began, the team built a framework on the whiteboard, placing the question, the variables, and the method into separate boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 framework 是「研究框架、基本架构」（第 2 个义项：学科或理论的基本结构）；句意：研究开始前，团队在白板上搭好框架，把问题、变量和方法放进各自的格子。

senses.title: A supporting structure
senses.definition: a structure of beams or bars that supports or encloses something
senses.definitionCN: 由梁或杆构成、用于支撑或围合某物的结构
senses.example: The steel framework holds up the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 钢架支撑着屋顶。
senses.why: Framework is literally frame + work, first recorded in the 1640s as 'structure for enclosing or supporting'. The frame is the working skeleton.
senses.whyCN: framework 字面是 frame + work，最早记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，义为“用于围合或支撑的结构”。frame 就是起作用的骨架。

senses.title: The basic structure of a system or theory
senses.titleCN: 体系或理论的基本结构
senses.definition: the set of main ideas and relations that gives shape to a system or theory
senses.definitionCN: 赋予体系或理论形状的一组主要观念与关系
senses.example: The theory provides a framework for understanding the data.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论提供了一个理解这些数据的框架。
senses.why: The figurative sense 'adjusted arrangement' is from 1816. Ideas also need a skeleton before details can be attached.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义“经过调整的安排”始于 1816 年。观念也需要骨架，细节才能挂上去。

senses.title: A set of rules or agreements
senses.definition: an agreed set of rules within which decisions or negotiations take place
senses.definitionCN: 决策或谈判在其中进行的一套约定规则
senses.example: The two countries signed a framework agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项框架协议。
senses.why: Rules form the structure within which later decisions are made, so a legal or political framework is a skeleton for action.
senses.whyCN: 规则构成后续决策在其中进行的结构，因此法律或政治框架就是行动的骨架。

senses.title: A building frame
senses.definition: the skeletal frame of a building before walls or cladding are added
senses.definitionCN: 尚未加墙体或外覆层之前的建筑骨架
senses.example: Workers erected the framework in three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们三周内搭起了构架。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense: the frame is put up first, and the rest of the building is attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的义项：先立起构架，建筑的其余部分再附着上去。

senses.title: A conceptual framework in research
senses.definition: the set of concepts and their assumed relationships that guides a study
senses.definitionCN: 指导一项研究的一组概念及其假定关系
senses.example: The paper sets out a conceptual framework for the study.
senses.exampleCN: 论文提出了本研究的理论框架。
senses.why: Research uses the word when concepts must be organized before evidence can be placed. The framework is the arrangement of ideas.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要先组织概念，才能安放证据，这时就用这个词。框架就是观念的安排。

senses.title: Computing: a software framework
senses.definition: a reusable set of code and conventions on which applications are built
senses.definitionCN: 用于构建应用的可复用代码与约定集合
senses.example: The team built the app on an open framework.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在一个开源框架上构建了应用。
senses.why: A software framework supplies the skeleton and calls the developer's code at set points, so the metaphor is exact.
senses.whyCN: 软件框架提供骨架，并在固定位置调用开发者的代码，因此这个比喻非常贴切。

senses.title: An organizational structure
senses.definition: the arrangement of roles, rules, and reporting lines in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 组织中角色、规则与汇报关系的安排
senses.example: The new framework gives local offices more power.
senses.exampleCN: 新架构给予地方办事处更多权力。
senses.why: An organization is held together by its structure of roles; change the framework and the parts relate differently.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠角色结构维系；改变框架，各部分的关系也随之改变。

senses.title: A story's frame
senses.definition: a story told inside another story, which frames it
senses.definitionCN: 套在另一个故事之中的故事，后者为前者提供外框
senses.example: The novel uses a story-within-a-story framework.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说采用故事套故事的叙事框架。
senses.why: Literature borrows the physical frame: an outer story surrounds and holds the inner one, as a picture frame holds a picture.
senses.whyCN: 文学借用了物理画框：外层故事包住并承托内层故事，正如画框承托画作。

intro.en: Framework is an English compound of frame and work, first recorded in the 1640s. Frame is older and partly Scandinavian, and its history is the key to the word.
intro.cn: framework 是 frame 与 work 的英语复合词，最早记录于 17 世纪 40 年代。frame 更古老，部分来自斯堪的纳维亚语，它的历史是理解这个词的关键。

items.en: First recorded as 'structure for enclosing or supporting', from frame (n.) + work (n.). The figurative sense 'adjusted arrangement' follows in 1816.
items.cn: 最早记录为“用于围合或支撑的结构”，由 frame（名词）+ work（名词）构成。比喻义“经过调整的安排”在 1816 年出现。

items.en: Frame is recorded as 'profit, benefit, advancement', then mid-13c. as 'a structure composed according to a plan', from the verb frame and partly from Scandinavian cognates such as Old Norse frami 'advancement'.
items.cn: frame 最早记录为“利润、益处、进展”，13 世纪中期指“按计划构成的结构”，来自动词 frame，部分来自斯堪的纳维亚同源词，如古诺尔斯语 frami“进展”。

items.en: Work is Middle English werk, from Old English weorc 'a deed, something done, action, business', also 'that which is made'. It descends from Proto-Germanic *werka- and PIE *werg- 'to do'.
items.cn: work 是中古英语 werk，来自古英语 weorc“行为、做过的事、行动、事务”，也指“被制成之物”。它源自原始日耳曼语 *werka- 和原始印欧语 *werg-“做”。

items.en: Frame develops the senses 'sustaining parts of a structure fitted together' (c. 1400) and 'enclosing border' (c. 1600), which make framework's physical sense possible.
items.cn: frame 发展出“拼合在一起的结构支撑部分”（约 1400 年）和“围合边框”（约 1600 年），使 framework 的物理义成为可能。

items.en: Framework extends to law, research, organizations and software. Frame of reference is from 1897 in mechanics, with its figurative sense from 1924.
items.cn: framework 延伸到法律、研究、组织和软件。frame of reference 在 1897 年出现于力学，比喻义始于 1924 年。

note.en: Look-alikes are the frame family; near meanings differ in whether they name a skeleton, a set of rules, or a background setting.
note.cn: 形近词是 frame 词族；近义词的区别在于指骨架、规则还是背景设定。

entries.definition: a border, a supporting structure, or a single picture. Framework is the whole working structure, while frame is one part or one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 边框、支撑结构，或单幅画面。framework 是整套起作用的构架，而 frame 是一部分或一个单元。

entries.definition: having a frame, or falsely made to look guilty. It is frame + -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 有边框的，或被构陷的。它是 frame + -ed。

entries.definition: the act of constructing a frame or of presenting something in a certain light.
entries.definitionCN: 构建框架的行为，或以某种角度呈现某物。

entries.definition: to place in a new frame or present in a new way. It is re- 'again' + frame.
entries.definitionCN: 重新装框，或以新方式表述。它是 re-“再次”+ frame。

entries.definition: the arrangement of parts in a whole. It is broader than framework and can describe anything from a building to a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中各部分的安排。它比 framework 更宽泛，可描述建筑，也可描述句子。

entries.definition: the supporting bones or frame of a body or building. It is more concrete and often temporary or bare.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或建筑的支撑骨架。它更具体，常指裸露或临时的骨架。

entries.definition: a set of connected parts working together. A framework is the structure of a system, not the system in operation.
